paragraphs.text: Ďalším bodom programu je spoločná rozprava o príprave zasadnutia Európskej rady: vyhlásenia Rady a Komisie – Príprava zasadnutia Európskej rady 18. – 19. júna 2026 (2026/2719(RSP)) a vyhlásenia Rady a Komisie – Budúcnosť hospodárskych vzťahov medzi EÚ a Čínou (2026/2761(RSP)).

Pripomínam vám, že pre túto prednostnú rozpravu nebude k dispozícii zoznam rečníkov. V prvom kole rečníkov v mene skupín budú vyzvaní vystúpiť poslanci, ktorí dostali rečnícky čas od svojich politických skupín alebo sekretariátu nezaradených poslancov. Pripomenie sa im pridelený rečnícky čas.

Sledujte, prosím, obrazovky v rokovacej sále, na ktorých sa zobrazí meno rečníka, ktorý má slovo a mená ďalších troch rečníkov. Hneď ako sa vaše meno zobrazí ako ďalšie v poradí, pripravte sa a choďte, prosím, do blízkosti hlavného rečníckeho pultu.

Počas rozpravy sa budú uplatňovať bežné pravidlá týkajúce sa modrých kariet a postup prihlásenia sa o slovo zdvihnutím ruky. Takisto pripomínam rečníkom a rečníčkam, že vzhľadom na aktuálne platné skúšobné opatrenie a presne stanovený čas ukončenia rozpravy bude potrebné prísne dodržiavať rečnícky čas.

interventions.speaker_label: Marilena Raouna, President-in-Office of the Council.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, honourable Members, Commissioner, tomorrow and Friday, EU leaders will meet in Brussels for the June European Council. Against a backdrop of profound geopolitical shifting and continued economic challenges, they will provide strategic guidance on a number of key issues, including Ukraine, the Middle East, European competitiveness and the next multiannual financial framework.

The European Council will send a strong message of unity and determination in support of Ukraine. Leaders will first hear from President Zelenskyy on the situation on the ground and the latest developments. Moreover, leaders are expected to discuss Russia's continued escalation and ongoing diplomatic efforts.

Recent developments demonstrate both Ukraine's resilience and the growing pressures facing Russia's war effort. This reinforces the need for the European Union to remain steadfast in its support for Ukraine and united in maintaining pressure on Russia.

Leaders will also welcome the opening of the first negotiating cluster on the fundamentals with Ukraine and with the Republic of Moldova two days ago. The Cyprus Presidency worked intensively since day one of its presidency and is very proud to have delivered this milestone moment in Ukraine's accession path and in Moldova's accession path.

Cyprus, as the Member State that continues to experience the devastating consequences of invasion and occupation, has a profound understanding of the importance of upholding sovereignty, territorial integrity, as well as the transformative power of the European project as the best security guarantee. And this unique perspective has driven our work on enlargement as well.

This discussion also comes in the wake of the EU–Western Balkans Summit in Tivat on 5 June, which provided renewed momentum for the enlargement agenda. Against this background, leaders are expected to reaffirm the European Union's unwavering commitment in supporting our Western Balkan partners on their path towards membership. The European Council will return on enlargement and reforms at its October meeting.

Another important topic on the leaders' agenda will be the ongoing crisis in the Middle East and the European Union's response. Leaders will welcome the agreement announced between the US and Iran for a ceasefire and a negotiating framework towards a sustained de-escalation across the region. In light of these developments, they will have an opportunity to discuss these developments, assess their implications for the Union and consider ways forward, while reaffirming the imperative need to ensure freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz and prevent further disruption to global markets, including for energy.

Leaders are also expected to call for the full implementation of the ceasefire in Lebanon, a permanent end to hostilities and full respect for Lebanon's sovereignty and territorial integrity, while reaffirming the European Union's continued support to Lebanon and its people.

The European Council will also address the catastrophic, unacceptable humanitarian situation in Gaza and the alarming escalation in the West Bank, calling for full respect of international law, international humanitarian law and reiterating the EU's commitment to a just, comprehensive and lasting peace on the two-state solution, in line with the relevant UN Security Council resolutions.

A further key issue concerns the next MFF, where advancing both horizontal and sectoral negotiations has been a top priority throughout the Cyprus Presidency. I am pleased to report that following months of intensive work, the Cyprus Presidency has delivered on the new MFF. On 11 June, we presented a revised negotiating box with figures. For the first time, leaders will discuss the next long-term budget on the basis of a concrete picture of the financial parameters underpinning the future MFF.

I am particularly pleased to inform this House that following yesterday's General Affairs Council, the Council under the Cyprus Presidency reached an agreement on all three key financing blocks of the future MFF: the NRPP, the ECF and Global Europe. This represents a decisive step in the negotiations, which brings us significantly closer to our shared objective of reaching an overall agreement before the end of the year. We anticipate that trilogues on the sectoral files will begin as soon as possible.

Let me now turn to competitiveness, which has remained central on the European agenda throughout this year and will continue to shape our work in the months ahead. On 24 April, in the margins of the informal European Council that took place in Nicosia, President Metsola, President Christodoulides and President von der Leyen signed the One Europe, One Market roadmap and this provides concrete actions and timelines. Against this backdrop, leaders will take stock of the progress achieved, as well as the implementation of the joint declaration on legislative priorities for 2026, together with the presidents of the European Parliament and Commission. Here, President Christodoulides will be presenting the main results of the Cyprus Presidency.

In the current economic environment, strengthening our competitiveness also requires further attention on the external dimension. Here, as in so many other areas, European unity remains our greatest strategic asset. Leaders will therefore discuss macroeconomic imbalances and other global economic challenges, with a view to developing a common understanding of the issues and stakes, and provide guidance to the Commission.

When it comes to China, our approach remains one of engagement and dialogue while firmly defending our economic and security interests, which are increasingly interconnected. We must continue to pursue a policy of de-risking, not decoupling, while ensuring a coherent and coordinated response.

On other important issues, leaders will address security and defence, including how to maintain momentum in the various strands of work here. Recent months have seen repeated drone incursions in EU airspace, including two serious incidents in Romania. These developments further underscore the urgency of advancing Europe's defence readiness agenda and strengthening our collective capacity to address emerging threats.

The European Council will revert to migration, ensuring that work continues at pace across all priority areas. The agreement reached this month on the Return Regulation, which complements the pact, whose entry into force was recently marked at an informal ministerial conference hosted by the Cyprus Presidency, is an important development.

Leaders will also devote attention to the challenge of illicit drugs on our societies. Moreover, they are expected to refer to the elections in Armenia, recognising the efforts of the Armenian authorities to safeguard the integrity of the electoral process amid mounting Russian pressure, and they will take stock of developments following the outbreak of the Ebola virus.

The Council will also take note of the Commission's recent communications on islands and coastal communities, which will be presented at a high-level conference hosted in Cyprus by the Cyprus Presidency on 26 June.

In closing, leaders will meet at a time when Europe faces no shortage of challenges but also the opportunities that present themselves. The breadth of the agenda before us reflects also the EU's capacity to act, to adapt and to deliver accordingly.

interventions.speaker_label: Maroš Šefčovič, Member of the Commission.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, Madam Minister Marilena, honourable Members, good morning. It is a pleasure to discuss with all of you the preparation of the upcoming European Council meeting. So to start with, the external affairs leaders will discuss the EU's continued support for Ukraine, notably the work on implementing the Ukraine support loan, with the first tranche of EUR 3.2 billion expected to be disbursed already next week. This follows the 21st package of sanctions and the recent positive developments regarding the accession process for both Ukraine and Moldova.
Leaders will also address the latest developments in the Middle East, including with regard to Iran, Lebanon and Palestine.

On Armenia, the leaders will discuss the EU support package under preparation in the face of the political and economic pressure on the country from Russia. The package will include immediate financial assistance worth over EUR 50 million, with further measures under preparation.

Leaders will also follow up on the eighth EU Western Balkans summit on 5 June. The Western Balkans belong in the EU, and enlargement is both a geostrategic imperative and long‑term investment in our stability and security.

Finally, leaders will discuss the need for EU‑wide cooperation in our response to the Ebola outbreak, following Commissioner Lahbib's visit to the Democratic Republic of Congo last week, where she announced EUR 16.5 million in additional EU support.

Closer to home, the leaders will have an exchange of views on the next multiannual financial framework, with a view to achieving concrete results before the end of 2026. This will be an opportunity to set the conditions for an agreement by the end of the year, and to provide a political steer on key issues, particularly the questions of the financial equation and the new own resources. Leaders will take stock of our shared commitment to strengthening competitiveness across our Union, in particular on the One Europe, One Market roadmap. Work on the Union's competitiveness starts at home, in particular by lowering energy costs; to this end, the Commission will present the review of the ETS in July, following our orientation debate in the College last week.

But it is also imperative that we tackle the external challenges to Europe's competitiveness, such as those caused by global macroeconomic imbalances. Leaders will discuss European defence and security, with the recent drone incidents in the Baltics and in Romania further underscoring the importance of our efforts in this domain. Work is advancing along different strands, including on SAFE and the defence readiness omnibus.

Leaders will take stock of progress on migration, with the pact on migration and asylum being fully applicable as of five days ago. Overall, irregular arrivals towards Europe are decreasing, but work should continue to fill any gaps in our procedures to enhance migration diplomacy.
And finally, leaders will call for the effective implementation of the EU drug strategy – of essential importance given the increased negative impact of drugs, and European health and security.

On China, let me stress that the Commission's overarching approach remains de-risking, as decoupling is neither desirable nor realistic. China remains a critical partner, and engagement in dialogue should intensify, albeit with a clear purpose of rebalancing. Ultimately, our trade and investment relationship must be reciprocal, fairer and underpinned by a level playing field. The EU should also continue its work on increasing the effectiveness of its trade defence policy, as well as strengthening diversification, including by making use of the numerous free trade agreements. This is essential for strengthening the resilience of our economy and enhancing the competitiveness of our industry.
Mr President, if you allow, I will stop here and I look forward to our discussion and exchanges this morning.

interventions.speaker_label: Manfred Weber, on behalf of the PPE Group.
interventions.speaker_role_in_transcript: on behalf of the PPE Group

paragraphs.text: Mr President, Commissioner, Council, dear friends in the European Parliament, first of all, let me pay respect to the Cypriot Presidency. What they have delivered in the last month under the leadership of Nikos Christodoulides and the team represented by you is remarkable. So thank you so much. You can be proud of this and Cyprus can be proud of this.

Ladies and gentlemen, dear friends, we are living in a moment of time where people feel huge, fundamental changes. It's a time of crisis and people are asking us for one thing, and that is to provide security. Our Europe must be a Europe that protects our citizens, and it starts economically with the question of Chinese economic power in this moment of time. We have a trade deficit with China, which comes to EUR 1 billion a day, EUR 360 billion a year. That is a trade deficit that is simply unacceptable. China is flooding European markets with their overcapacity and that has to stop.

We, as the European People's Party, stand for free trade – no doubt about this – but we need, as the Commissioner already said, reciprocity, public procurement. When we finance investments with EU funds, it is not understandable why Chinese are benefiting from this if we do not have the same principle in China. We need a level playing field; we have to do this on the basis of the WTO – no doubt about this – but we have to tell the Chinese that subsidies are not part of fair trade. We also have to be clear on our sovereignty when it is about critical networks. The next development on 6G network in Europe should be only a European network. We have to be sovereign on these issues. You also have to ask the business sector to please stop the naivety when it is about intellectual property rights, when it is about the question of Taiwan. Please be aware that things can fundamentally change. These are the considerations when it is about China.

Yesterday, we voted on the US deal here in this House. Thank God we now have clarity and predictability for our business. That is also a chance to restart. The G7 meeting in Évian gives us a chance for this to restart the kind of economic NATO thinking that, together with the Americans, we should think about how to answer the economic model of China. There is a global question in front of us, and I want to reconnect with our American friends.

Dear friends, that is all embedded in the question of competitiveness, because, on the other hand, we have to see that China is a strong competitor. So that is why it is not only about protecting ourselves, but also standing up and investing in competitiveness on the European level. The second issue I want to mention is about protecting ourselves and external security, and there enlargement contributes to our external security.

Yesterday, dear friends, it was impressive to see that the President of Montenegro, when we speak so much about details of legislation here in this Chamber, he speaks about freedom, about history, about being part of Europe. These ideas of such a country like Montenegro, of leaders like the President of the country of Montenegro, this new fundamental thinking about what Europe really means is so important for all of us. So bringing Ukraine close to us is an investment in our security. Ladies and gentlemen, that is on the table for the Council, and we see positive momentum in this moment of time. You can be proud of this and Cyprus can be proud of this.

It's a time of crisis and people are asking us for one thing, and that is to provide security. Our Europe must be a Europe that protects our citizens, and it starts economically with the question of Chinese economic power in this moment of time. We have a trade deficit with China, which comes to EUR 1 billion a day, EUR 360 billion a year. That is a trade deficit that is simply unacceptable. China is flooding European markets with their overcapacity and that has to stop.

We, as the European People's Party, stand for free trade – no doubt about this – but we need, as the Commissioner already said, reciprocity, public procurement. When we finance investments with EU funds, it is not understandable why Chinese are benefiting from this if we do not have the same principle in China. We need a level playing field; we have to do this on the basis of the WTO – no doubt about this – but we have to tell the Chinese that subsidies are not part of fair trade. We also have to be clear on our sovereignty when it is about critical networks. The next development on 6G network in Europe should be only a European network. Yesterday, we voted on the US deal here in this House. Thank God we now have clarity and predictability for our business. That is also a chance to restart. interventions.speaker_label: Iratxe García Pérez, en nombre del Grupo S&D.

paragraphs.text: Señor presidente, he escuchado con atención el discurso del señor Weber y, si cualquier ciudadano europeo prestara la misma atención, simplificando, podría tener el mensaje de que, para Europa, «China mal, los Estados Unidos bien».

Simplifiquemos, ese ha sido el mensaje. Y yo creo que, en este mundo tan complejo, debemos entender que las relaciones exteriores, las relaciones económicas y las relaciones de comercio son mucho más complejas que esos mensajes y tenemos que ser serios a la hora, sobre todo, de hablar de la soberanía europea para desempeñar un papel fundamental en este mundo tan difícil y tan complejo para los ciudadanos, porque eso es exactamente lo que estamos viviendo.

Hoy, algunos celebran el acuerdo entre los Estados Unidos e Irán. Y sí, toda posibilidad de paz es una buena noticia, pero no olvidemos la verdad. Después de más de 7 000 muertos, ciudades destruidas y millones de personas golpeadas por la inflación, volvemos al punto de partida.

Hay quienes miraron hacia otro lado durante una guerra ilegal e inmoral impulsada por Trump y Netanyahu. Hoy vemos el resultado de aquellas promesas de seguridad e incluso de democracia. Y ahora deberían responder: ¿dónde está esa democracia prometida a los ciudadanos y al pueblo de Irán? Porque la democracia no nace de los bombardeos, no se construye sobre escombros, no florece entre miles de muertos.

Resulta grotesco escuchar a Trump vender como una victoria la reapertura del estrecho de Ormuz. ¿Qué victoria? Ormuz estaba abierto antes de la guerra. Presume de haber resuelto un problema que él mismo ha creado. Y, mientras tanto, las petroleras acumulan beneficios extraordinarios y millones de familias pagan facturas más altas, hipotecas más caras y una cesta de la compra más costosa. Y le pregunto a la Comisión Europea: ¿dónde está la propuesta para gravar los beneficios caídos del cielo?

Hay que aprender la lección. La verdadera respuesta europea no es más dependencia del petróleo y del gas, es acelerar el Pacto Verde Europeo e invertir en energías renovables. Pero los dobles estándares no terminan ahí: ciudadanos europeos fueron humillados y maltratados tras el asalto a una flotilla humanitaria rumbo a Gaza y el Consejo es incapaz siquiera de sancionar a Ben‑Gvir. La misma impunidad que permite que continúe el genocidio en Gaza, la misma cobardía que vemos con la Corte Penal Internacional cuando Trump sanciona a jueces internacionales por hacer su trabajo y ustedes se niegan a activar el estatuto de bloqueo para protegerlos. Dicen defender el Estado de Derecho, pero lo abandonan cuando el agresor se llama Trump.

Y esta semana se da un paso más grave. El Partido Popular y la extrema derecha aprobarán un Reglamento que abre la puerta a centros de detención fuera de la Unión Europea, agujeros negros donde podrán enviarse incluso a niños.

Señor Weber, cuando visitan al papa León XIV, ¿le cuentan estos planes? ¿Le explican que pretenden enviar seres humanos a campos de deportación en países que violan los derechos humanos? El papa dijo en España que nadie puede arrodillarse ante el Señor y despreciar al hermano. Y recordó que discriminar a una persona por su origen vulnera la dignidad de todos los seres humanos. No son palabras revolucionarias. Son valores cristianos, los mismos valores que ustedes dicen defender mientras pactan con la extrema derecha políticas que los pisotean.

Y mientras erosionan estos valores, veo que es difícil para ustedes sostener esa dignidad cristiana de la que hablan. Porque la pregunta sigue siendo la misma: ¿queremos una Europa subordinada a otros, hostil con los migrantes y resignada ante las injusticias? ¿O queremos una Europa fiel a sí misma?
La socialdemocracia elige una Europa del Derecho internacional y más fuerte y no vamos a permitir que ustedes la sigan desmontando. ¡Cómo les ha molestado!

paragraphs.text: Tisztelt Elnök Úr! A Patrióták vezérelve, hogy az uniós döntéseknek az európai embereket kell szolgálniuk, így a következő hétéves költségvetésnek is. A megvitatásra kerülő tervezet ezer sebből vérzik, mert Brüsszel a közös agrárpolitika és a kohéziós politika forrásait csökkentené, így nem lehet versenyképes Európát építeni.

Elutasítjuk az uniós bürokrácia bővítésére irányuló forrásnövelést is. Az európai emberek pénzét ne használják további központosításra. Továbbá ellenzünk minden jogállamisági feltételrendszert a költségvetésben. Az uniós források nem válhatnak a Bizottság ideológiai nyomásgyakorlásának eszközévé. Ahogy nem lehet a demokráciát a demokrácia korlátozásával erősíteni.

Ezért elfogadhatatlan az új magyar kormány visszamenőleges hatályú, személyre szabott alkotmánymódosítása. Ennek egyetlen célja, hogy kizárjon egy politikai szereplőt, Orbán Viktort demokratikus választásokon való indulásból. Ez teljesen példátlan az európai jogi hagyományban. Akik eddig folyamatosan vészharangokat kongattak a jogállamisággal kapcsolatban, most mélyen hallgatnak. Sokat elárul ez a kettős mércéről.

A tagállamok vezetői azzal is tisztában kell legyenek, hogy Ukrajna uniós csatlakozása veszélyt jelent úgy a mezőgazdaság, a munkaerőpiac, mint polgáraink biztonságára nézve. Most mégis úgy nyitották meg a csatlakozási tárgyalásokat, hogy a legalapvetőbb feltételek nem teljesülnek.

Ahogy a múlt héten hatályba lépett migrációs paktum továbbra sem a megoldás, hanem a probléma része. Nem teszi az Uniót felkészültebbé egy esetleges újabb migrációs válság kezelésére. A Patrióták határozottan elutasítják ezt a paktumot. A mi álláspontunk világos: meg kell védenünk Európa külső határait, és meg kell állítanunk az illegális migrációt, hogy megőrizzük Európa kulturális identitását és polgárainak biztonságát.
Mi, Patrióták, gyökeres változást szeretnénk, egy biztonságosabb, versenyképesebb és józanabb Európát.

interventions.speaker_label: Nicola Procaccini, a nome del gruppo ECR.

paragraphs.text: Signor Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, la priorità che deve guidare i leader europei nel prossimo Consiglio è la competitività strategica del continente. Ma la competitività non si fabbrica negli uffici di Bruxelles, la si fa sul campo, la si favorisce con il buon senso e la si difende con la fermezza.

Ciò significa, per cominciare, cambiare atteggiamento nei confronti del regime di Pechino. L'Europa deve rispondere con decisione alla concorrenza sleale, al mismatch delle materie prime critiche e a una totale mancanza di reciprocità che rischiano di soffocare il nostro tessuto produttivo.

Ma non può esistere uno spazio economico senza la giusta cornice di sicurezza. Ciò significa, quindi, non deflettere dal sostegno al popolo ucraino, non deflettere dalla pressione politica sul regime iraniano. Sicurezza significa anche essere in grado di difendere i confini europei dall'immigrazione illegale di massa.

Siamo a poche ore da un voto storico. Con il nuovo regolamento rimpatri l'Europa torna padrona del proprio destino. Chi non ha diritto all'asilo politico tornerà velocemente da dove è venuto, mentre potrà essere accolto chi ne ha davvero diritto, chi lo merita per le proprie capacità lavorative e per la volontà di condividere il nostro sistema di valori.

In passato ha prevalso l'utopia sinistra dei confini aperti a tutti. Il risultato è stato migliaia di morti in mare, l'escalation del traffico di esseri umani, il degrado e il pericolo nelle nostre città.

Solo pochi anni fa, quando noi conservatori in quest'Aula e il governo italiano in Consiglio chiedevamo di passare dalla ricollocazione dei migranti in Europa alla gestione del fenomeno migratorio fuori dai confini europei, venivamo derisi, schiacciati da una maggioranza sorda di fronte alla ragione.
Oggi una nuova maggioranza, ispirata dal buon senso, sta per rimuovere una delle spine più dolorose dal cuore dei popoli europei. Quindi facciamo la cosa giusta per noi e per chi verrà dopo di noi.

paragraphs.text: Monsieur le Président, Monsieur le Commissaire, Madame la Ministre, chers collègues, ce sommet européen se tient alors que les États-Unis et l'Iran vont signer un accord de paix. Cette guerre absurde, aux conséquences désastreuses pour la sécurité du monde et le pouvoir d'achat des Européens, est venue rappeler les enjeux qui attendent l'Europe. Parce que, qu'est-ce qui se passe aujourd'hui dans le monde? Qu'est-ce qui explique les agissements de Trump ou de Xi Jinping? Ce qui se passe, c'est une guerre froide qui ne dit pas son nom. Deux puissances, la Chine et les États-Unis, qui se disputent le contrôle du monde.

Eh bien, chers collègues, je refuse que l'Europe s'aligne sur l'une ou l'autre de ces puissances. Je refuse que l'Europe serve des intérêts qui ne sont pas d'abord les siens. Notre destin, c'est la voie de notre indépendance. Indépendance énergétique, mais aussi indépendance économique, technologique et donc indépendance géopolitique. Chers collègues, le prochain sommet nécessite de la hauteur de vue et de la vision. L'Europe fait face à elle-même et elle a encore le choix. Mais le temps presse. Et quand je parle d'indépendance, voici ce que j'attends de ce sommet.

Premièrement, la fin de notre vassalité heureuse. Alors oui, bien sûr, on doit travailler avec la Chine et les États-Unis. Oui, on doit commercer avec eux. Oui, on doit se retrouver sur la défense d'intérêts que nous pouvons avoir en commun. Les terres rares, par exemple. Mais on ne doit pas être à leur botte. Jamais. Pas aujourd'hui et pas demain. Deuxièmement, la poursuite de notre soutien à l'Ukraine parce qu'il y va de notre propre sécurité.

Troisièmement, l'accélération de notre agenda de compétitivité et d'innovation. C'est un point central qu'a montré l'affaire Anthropic ce week-end. L'accès aux technologies de pointe est une nouvelle forme de guerre économique que nous livrent les États-Unis et la Chine. Et pour y répondre, on n'a pas 36 solutions. On doit compter sur nous-mêmes, sur notre souveraineté technologique, avec des entreprises européennes de pointe dans l'intelligence artificielle et dans des secteurs d'avenir. Et pour que cela soit possible, c'est ma quatrième demande, il faut de l'argent, du financement. Il nous faut un budget européen à la hauteur de nos ambitions et une vraie politique de libération des capitaux européens.

Alors, vous l'avez compris, chers collègues, pour être respectée dans le monde d'aujourd'hui, il est temps pour l'Europe d'assumer le langage de la puissance. Mais une puissance qui nous ressemble, ferme sur nos principes, lucide quant aux rapports de force, jamais brutale.

Premièrement, la fin de notre vassalité heureuse. Alors oui, bien sûr, on doit travailler avec la Chine et les États-Unis. Oui, on doit commercer avec eux. Oui, on doit se retrouver sur la défense d'intérêts que nous pouvons avoir en commun. Les terres rares, par exemple. Mais on ne doit pas être à leur botte. Jamais. Pas aujourd'hui et pas demain. Deuxièmement, la poursuite de notre soutien à l'Ukraine parce qu'il y va de notre propre sécurité.

Troisièmement, l'accélération de notre agenda de compétitivité et d'innovation. C'est un point central qu'a montré l'affaire Anthropic ce week-end. L'accès aux technologies de pointe est une nouvelle forme de guerre économique que nous livrent les États-Unis et la Chine. Et pour y répondre, on n'a pas 36 solutions. On doit compter sur nous-mêmes, sur notre souveraineté technologique, avec des entreprises européennes de pointe dans l'intelligence artificielle et dans des secteurs d'avenir. Et pour que cela soit possible, c'est ma quatrième demande, il faut de l'argent, du financement. Il nous faut un budget européen à la hauteur de nos ambitions et une vraie politique de libération des capitaux européens.

Alors, vous l'avez compris, chers collègues, pour être respectée dans le monde d'aujourd'hui, il est temps pour l'Europe d'assumer le langage de la puissance. Mais une puissance qui nous ressemble, ferme sur nos principes, lucide quant aux rapports de force, jamais brutale.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, colleagues, in 2022, Europe faced a dramatic explosion of gas prices after Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine. The consequences were inflation, a cost-of-living crisis and insecurity amongst our citizens. In 2026, this time Trump started a war against Iran: another skyrocketing of fossil fuel prices, again inflation going up, prices going up, insecurity for our citizens.

The reasons are so crystal clear. Our immense dependency on fossil fuels is not only making us weaker; it is making us poorer every single day. Common people do not know how to make ends meet anymore, while at the same time fossil fuel companies are making record profits.

So it is on them but, colleagues, it is also on us, because instead of pushing for the only logical thing – actually ending our dependencies on fossil fuels – we let the far right, and also part of the EPP, run around claiming that all of this is just the problem of the ETS.

The ETS and the Green Deal, the plan to build European sovereignty and economic success, are the single most powerful tool to fight against exactly these fossil fuel dependencies. That is why a green Europe means a strong Europe. And if Europe wants to be a global actor, to stand up to autocracies in the world, including China, we have to become world champions in this green future.

I cannot hear all the doom talking anymore, colleagues. Yes, we are in a tricky situation, but if this continent has proven one thing in the past, it is its ability to master crises if we work together. So the time for complaining is over. Let's fucking do this! Let's fight for a green and strong Europe!

paragraphs.text: Monsieur le président, Madame la Ministre, Monsieur le Commissaire, vous voyez ce petit bout de Lego? C'est tout ce qu'il reste d'une école maternelle au sud de Beyrouth, pulvérisée par une bombe israélienne. J'ai promis aux sœurs qui gèrent cette école de le ramener ici avec cette question: pourquoi l'Union européenne ne fait-elle rien face à ces atrocités? Et puisque vous refusez de voir ces atrocités, je vous ai aussi apporté ce débris de missile israélien qui a frappé un centre pour personnes en situation de handicap. Puisque vous refusez de les voir, je vous parlerai ici, dans cet hémicycle, de celles et ceux que j'ai rencontrés au Liban. Dali, treize ans, qui a perdu sa mère, une partie de son crâne et de ses jambes sous une bombe israélienne. Danan, quatre ans, amputé des deux jambes, qui a perdu ses parents dans l'explosion de sa maison.

Monsieur le Commissaire, que leur direz-vous? Que l'UE a préféré tergiverser plutôt que d'en finir avec sa complicité? Douze enfants sont tués ou blessés chaque jour au Liban. Encore plus depuis le prétendu cessez-le-feu du 17 avril. Alors comment croire que celui annoncé cette semaine sera respecté? En quelques jours, l'armée israélienne a d'ailleurs déjà ciblé Beyrouth et le sud du Liban. Le sang de ces enfants, Monsieur le Commissaire, Madame la Ministre, sera aussi sur vos mains tant que vous refusez de sanctionner Netanyahou et de suspendre l'accord d'association entre l'Union européenne et Israël, comme le demandent plus d'un million de citoyens européens. Si les grands de ce monde, réunis au G7 ou au Conseil européen, avaient ne serait-ce qu'une once d'humanité, voilà ce qu'ils feraient plutôt que d'énièmes palabres, pour qu'un jour les enfants du Liban apprennent de nouveau à lire dans des écoles plutôt qu'à se protéger des bombes.

paragraphs.text: Herr Präsident! Europa erlebt eine Welle der Gewalt von illegalen Einwanderern gegen uns Europäer. Jeden Tag neue Horrormeldungen – Nürnberg, Halle, Rom. Und gestern die Veröffentlichung des Berichts über die Verbrechen von Einwanderern an 250 000 weißen Mädchen der Arbeiterklasse – alles geschehen, während Großbritannien Mitglied der Europäischen Union war.
Der Rat müsste sich für eine europaweite Untersuchung dieser Verbrechen einsetzen; Thema ist diese Verbrechenswelle beim Treffen der Staats- und Regierungschefs aber nicht.
Stattdessen: EU-Erweiterung. Wieder ist die Ukraine auf der Tagesordnung. Die Ukraine wäre mit ihrem Beitritt sofort und mit Abstand der größte Nettoempfänger der gesamten Europäischen Union.
Wir wollen zur Ukraine sehr gute Handelsbeziehungen. Wir wollen mit der Ukraine eine sehr gute Partnerschaft in der Zukunft, aber darüber hinausgehen wollen wir nicht.

interventions.speaker_label: Maroš Šefčovič, Member of the Commission.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, I will, of course, respect the time allocated to me, and I will be very, very brief. But I will touch upon the topics which are most frequently mentioned by the parliamentary leaders, Mr Weber, Mr Procaccini, Ms Reintke, Ms Hayer, referring to our forthcoming discussions and the need to reset, rebalance our relationship with China. I want to reassure you that this is exactly the proposal the Commission is undertaking, and we would like to base it around a couple of principles.

First, we want to have much more regular engagement with our Chinese counterparts to make sure that we find the solutions to how to reverse what we described also to them as the unsustainable growing trade deficit between the European Union and China.

We want to rebalance our trade. We will push for more reciprocity and, of course, we will work very hard with our Member States and our stakeholders to put more emphasis on diversification, because we know that all dependencies are very expensive, and we pay a very high price, especially in the field of energy.

What would be very important – and what I appreciate in the interventions from all political leaders – is the call for unity, because unity is our most precious currency. You heard me saying this when I was discussing other strategic relationships with our partners. But I would say that in this particular case, this is even more important.

If you allow me to respond to Ms García Pérez and Ms Manon Aubry, I just would like to underline once again, and very, very clearly, that we all agree that the EU remains strongly opposed to Israel's settlement policies and activities. They are illegal under international law, they constitute an obstacle to peace, and they undermine the viability of the two‑state solution.

As both Ms Aubry and Ms García Pérez recalled, we already tabled very concrete proposals in this regard, to suspend the trade-related provisions of the EU‑Israel Association Agreement. We had a discussion on this topic again on Monday among the foreign ministers, where we called for the Council to work on the necessary qualified majority. I believe that there are the best endeavours from the Cypriot Presidency to achieve that result.
If you allow me, Mr President, because the debate is rather long, I would reserve the remaining time for the end of the discussion.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, firstly I'd like to congratulate the Commission and the Council for the remarkable progress on enlargement made over the course of recent weeks. This is also the result of the fact that the European Commission has strategically prioritised enlargement since the beginning of its term in office, understanding that the safer, the more stable, the more secure our neighbours (the EU candidate countries) are, the better for the people in these countries and the better also for the European Union. Let us continue to help candidate countries to reform, modernise, become stronger, fulfil accession criteria and join us as soon as possible.

Secondly, thank you very much to the Cypriot Presidency of the Council for the progress made on the multiannual financial framework. It is very good that we now have a negotiating box in the Council, so that the Council can also start to make progress in view of reaching a Council's position, as the Parliament already has a position for the upcoming negotiations.

The situation is the following: we know the challenges Europe is facing: competitiveness, defence, security, Ukraine, enlargement. The question is whether we are ready to finance these challenges properly. And unfortunately, the message that we are receiving from the Council so far is worrying. We say competitiveness is a priority; the Council proposes to cut funding for competitiveness, research, innovation, strategic investments. We say security and defence are important, and then the Council is proposing to cut funding there. The Council correctly identifies Europe's challenges, but unfortunately it fails to provide the resources needed to address them. We cannot do more with less. A bigger budget should not be a scope in itself …

political_group.label: PPE
political_group.name: Group of the European People's Party (Christian Democrats)

paragraphs.text: Panie Przewodniczący! Droga Rado! Panie Komisarzu! Po raz kolejny usłyszałem tutaj, że potrzebujemy więcej zielonych rozwiązań, to będzie lepiej – tego już nie da się słuchać. To jest dokładnie tak samo – my, Polacy, dobrze to pamiętamy – jak było w Związku Sowieckim, że ciągle twierdzono, że jeszcze więcej tych samych rozwiązań, to będzie w końcu lepiej.

Ja tylko przypomnę, że Unia Europejska wdrożyła pełno tych zielonych rozwiązań. No i jakie mamy efekty? No to Zielonych muszę zapytać, jakie mamy efekty? Przemysł upada. Mamy najdroższy prąd na świecie. Nawet perła w koronie, to znaczy przemysł samochodowy w Unii Europejskiej, przegrywa z Chińczykami na własnym boisku. A Wy mówicie: jeszcze więcej tego samego. Rolnictwo upada. I do tego mamy umowę z Mercosurem, mamy zaostrzenie polityki klimatycznej i jeszcze teraz nowe WRF, gdzie mamy mieć mniej środków na rolnictwo. Przecież to skończy się katastrofą.

Do tego oczywiście przestępczość rośnie. Ja przed chwilą usłyszałem z ust przewodniczącej Lewicy, że będziemy nowym rozwiązaniem zmuszać migrantów do tego, żeby przesuwali się w miejsca, gdzie oni nie chcą być - poza Unię Europejską. A na czym polega pakt migracyjny? Pakt migracyjny polega dokładnie na tym samym, tylko wewnątrz Unii Europejskiej. My też będziemy przesuwali migrantów dokładnie do tych państw, gdzie oni nie chcą być, bo inaczej by sobie poszli, dobrze wiecie do jakich państw. Do tych, gdzie mają najlepiej. Więc to jest hipokryzja do kwadratu.

Dodatkowo słyszałem i to jest prawda, tutaj trzeba się zgodzić z PPE, że Europa chce więcej bezpieczeństwa. I to jest prawda. Tylko problem polega na tym, że my nie będziemy mieć więcej bezpieczeństwa bez konkurencyjności, jeżeli nie wyciągniemy naszej gospodarki. Dlatego trzeba zatrzymać ETS, bo ETS to jest szaleństwo, które doprowadziło nas dzisiaj do sytuacji, w której udział gospodarki Unii Europejskiej na świecie regularnie spada, gdzie nasz udział w decydowaniu politycznym na świecie regularnie spada. I dlatego jeszcze raz trzeba powiedzieć: stop ETS, i zobaczycie, że wtedy od razu nasza gospodarka się ruszy.

paragraphs.text: Voorzitter, ik wil het toch even kort hebben over het MFK en de houding van onze vrekkige vier. Toen vorige week minister Heinen de begroting zag, riep hij meteen: “Onacceptabel en onbetaalbaar!”. De bekende zuinige reflex. Maar met de vinger op de knip ontneem je jezelf de kans om te investeren in de toekomst. Heinen en de andere vrekkige landen willen pas spreken als er hervormingen liggen, terwijl de realiteit heel simpel is: hervormingen kosten geld.

Een boer die moet verduurzamen, help je niet met een bezuiniging. Die help je met perspectief en middelen. De wereld buiten Europa wacht niet op ons. Een Europees defensiesysteem kost geld. Een toekomstbestendige economie kost geld. Een sterk en Europees energiesysteem kost geld. De internationale markt is grillig en de leveringen zijn onzeker. Dat is het moment om te kiezen voor Europese autonomie en innovatie. De kosten gaan voor de baten uit. Dat hoort bij visie en leiderschap. Laten we de toekomst niet wegbezuinigen. De wereld staat niet stil. Wij moeten meebewegen.

paragraphs.text: Hartstikke goed, maar ik vind de Nederlandse houding gewoon altijd typisch. We zien dat eens in de zoveel jaar: altijd heel stoer hoge verwachtingen creëren en dan zelf teleurstelling creëren richting Europa. Je weet gewoon dat, als je wilt hervormen, je ook met investeringen moet komen, want die hervormingen kosten geld. Ook prima dat lidstaten dat individueel doen, maar ik denk dat we, zoals de heer Weber zegt, veel sterker staan als we ook een NAVO creëren op het gebied van economie, op het gebied van de chips en op het gebied van verduurzaming, en dat doe je gewoon veel beter vanuit Europa. Dat is in het belang van Nederland en uiteindelijk in het belang van ons allemaal.

We zien dat eens in de zoveel jaar: altijd heel stoer hoge verwachtingen creëren en dan zelf teleurstelling creëren richting Europa. Je weet gewoon dat, als je wilt hervormen, je ook met investeringen moet komen, want die hervormingen kosten geld. Ook prima dat lidstaten dat individueel doen, maar ik denk dat we, zoals de heer Weber zegt, veel sterker staan als we ook een NAVO creëren op het gebied van economie, op het gebied van de chips en op het gebied van verduurzaming, en dat doe je gewoon veel beter vanuit Europa. Dat is in het belang van Nederland en uiteindelijk in het belang van ons allemaal.

paragraphs.text: Senhor Presidente, ao contrário do que diz o PPE, as preocupações dos trabalhadores e dos povos ficam à porta desta reunião do Conselho Europeu, mas em nome desses povos serão tomadas decisões contra os seus interesses. Habitação, combate à pobreza, aumento de salários e elevação das condições de vida, apoio aos setores produtivos e aos pequenos produtores; nada disto estará na agenda.

Os preços da energia e dos combustíveis penalizam os povos com o aumento do custo de vida. Do Conselho Europeu, nem uma palavra de condenação da agressão dos Estados Unidos ao Irão que provocou essa situação, nem uma medida para travar as multinacionais da energia que se aproveitam dela para acumular lucros.

O aumento das taxas de juro decidido pelo BCE aumenta o custo de vida dos povos e multiplica os lucros da banca. O Conselho Europeu não vê nisso assunto a discutir, mas não faltam medidas para favorecer as multinacionais e os grupos económicos, para perseguir migrantes, para prolongar a guerra na Ucrânia e insistir na confrontação com a Rússia. Falam de Gaza e do Líbano, sem beliscar Israel, como se isso permitisse pôr fim ao genocídio do povo palestiniano e travar a agressão ao Líbano.

paragraphs.text: Herr Präsident! Auf den völkerrechtswidrigen Krieg Russlands haben wir mit Sanktionen reagiert, die unsere Abhängigkeit von Donald Trumps schmutzigem Frackinggas erhöht haben; auf die völkerrechtswidrigen Kriege der USA und Israels, da gab es nur Schweigen bei den Spitzen der EU.

Und jetzt lassen wir uns von den USA in einen Wirtschaftskrieg mit China hineintreiben. Als mein Land – Deutschland – viele Jahre über hohe Exportüberschüsse verfügte, haben wir das immer damit verteidigt, dass das die große deutsche Ingenieurskunst sei. Jetzt bei China schreien wir auf. Und selbstverständlich gibt es Überkapazitäten, zum Beispiel beim Stahl. Aber China hat auch mit kluger strategischer Industriepolitik immer mehr Kontrolle über Wertschöpfungsketten erlangt – bei kritischen Rohstoffen, bei Halbleitern.

Deswegen sollten wir viel mehr vom Beispiel Chinas lernen, dass eine Politik, die den Rückzug des Staates aus der Wirtschaft verkündet, nicht funktioniert und das Scheitern des deutsch-französischen Kampfjets zeigt, dass der Weg der Europäische Union, vor allem in Rüstung zu investieren, scheitern muss. Wir müssen in strategische Zukunftssektoren investieren.

paragraphs.text: Herr Präsident! Kein Haushalt der Welt kann einfach wachsen, ohne demokratisch kontrolliert zu werden. Der MFR für die nächsten sieben Jahre sieht allerdings das vor: Wachstum in unglaublicher Höhe, und unter dem Vorwand von noch mehr Flexibilität sollen demokratische Kontrollmechanismen eingeschränkt werden. Wie funktioniert das? Indem die EU faktisch Steuern einführt, die sie als sogenannte Eigenmittel framt.

Hier kommt es tatsächlich dem Rat zugute, dass es hier Widerstand gibt. Und es gibt Gott sei Dank Widerstand – selbst vom deutschen Bundeskanzler. Insofern kann ich Sie nur ermutigen: Bleiben Sie stark bei Ihrer Position, dass diese Eigenmittel in der Größe nicht eingeführt werden.

Herr Weber, Sie haben eben gesagt, es sei gut, dass es aktuell Freiheits- und Demokratieentwicklungen in ganz Europa geben würde. Ich möchte Sie daran erinnern, dass es demnächst eine Landtagswahl in Sachsen-Anhalt gibt. Sie wird es auch freuen, dass die AfD in den Umfragen bei über 40 % liegt. Und die WELT schreibt über den scheidenden CDU-Ministerpräsidenten: Schulze will sich zum Ministerpräsidenten unabhängig vom Ergebnis wählen lassen. Genau so …

paragraphs.text: Mr President, dear colleagues, Commissioner, Council, the multiannual financial framework is a political statement about what kind of Europe we want. It is up to the pro-European groups in this Parliament to ensure that we live up to this responsibility.

When it comes to the green transition, we cannot afford to go backwards. What's proposed by the Council – with a 35 % climate spending target across the MFF – is not ambitious for the sake of the ambition; it's a bare minimum. We already see communities and citizens paying a very high price for the climate crisis. Let's, with this coming budget, limit further cost for humans and the economy.

The same goes for the 'do no significant harm' principle. Let's make sure it's not just a little box we tick, but actually a tool to ensure the money goes in the right direction. And the same goes for the rule of law and for our fundamental values. Let's make it count.

The overall size of the MFF must be ambitious. A weak budget delivers weak policies. We cannot cut back when it comes to green action or when it comes to our most vulnerable citizens and community. They depend on EU investments.

Finally, Council, when you sit around the table and negotiate the coming MFF in the meeting, don't forget you have to agree with us in this House. That also comes on our shoulders, dear colleagues – that we actually look at each other, the pro-European parties, and live up to the ambitions we have for a strong Europe and a strong budget.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, Minister, Commissioner Šefčovič, I only have one minute for a very long agenda in the Council, so I'll concentrate on competitiveness to once again ask for speed and urgency.

On speed – okay, Europe is moving a bit faster, but the rest of the world is moving at warp speed and we keep falling behind, basically because we are massively underestimating the gigantic impact of AI and its exponential growth – massively. The events of the past few weeks should be a wake-up call – I'm not sure they were.

This is where boldness comes in; if competitiveness is really our priority, we cannot put AI as a sub, sub, sub-point of the Council agenda, or a footnote of recycled funds in the MFF. AI should be the main point of the agenda because AI's challenge is essential for Europe and should be treated as an emergency.

Therefore, I urge this Council to make bold choices now – change the MFF to multiply investment in AI and remove regulatory barriers that make it impossible to train AI models in Europe. It is hard, I know, it means making tough choices about the MFF. Some things we like will get less money so that the things we need get more money. It is Europe's long-term relevance that is stake. Be bold, there is still time ...

paragraphs.text: Vielen Dank, Herr Präsident, auch für das Verständnis. Herr Kommissar, Frau Ratsvertreterin, liebe Kolleginnen und Kollegen! Ich möchte gerne zur Beziehung Europas zu China sprechen; das ist ja auch eines der wichtigen Themen jetzt auf der Tagesordnung für das Gipfeltreffen. Ich denke, das Wichtigste ist, dass wir in Europa nicht naiv sein dürfen, sondern dass wir unsere Möglichkeiten nutzen müssen und uns an die neuen Herausforderungen anpassen müssen.

China ist ein schwieriger Partner. Das spüren wir hier im Europäischen Parlament, aber vor allen Dingen spüren das unsere Unternehmen zu Hause. Wir dürfen nicht zulassen – unser Fraktionsvorsitzender hat es gesagt –, dass chinesische Staatsubventionen und die chinesische Überproduktion unseren Markt einfach nur kaputt machen. Wir wollen europäische Wertschöpfung, wir wollen Wettbewerb, wir wollen Handel, aber er muss fair sein.

Auch China ist vom Welthandel abhängig, und China braucht auch unseren europäischen Markt mit 450 Millionen Verbraucherinnen und Verbrauchern. Als Europäische Union dürfen wir uns deshalb nicht klein machen …

paragraphs.text: Monsieur le Président, les agriculteurs sont habitués aux mauvaises nouvelles de Bruxelles. La baisse annoncée du futur budget de la PAC, les traités de libre-échange, les contraintes. Ils viennent d'apprendre l'officialisation du début des négociations pour l'entrée de l'Ukraine dans l'Union européenne. L'Ukraine est un géant agricole, nous le savons tous, qui est déjà favorisé par l'Union européenne, par un contrat d'association qui provoque une concurrence totalement déloyale.

L'entrée de l'Ukraine dans l'Union européenne provoquerait pour nos agriculteurs une véritable catastrophe. Dans le marché unique, ce serait une concurrence totalement déloyale sur de nombreuses productions, en plus avec un non-respect de nos normes. Et puis, bien évidemment, dans l'état actuel de la PAC, ce serait pour l'ensemble des pays des 27 une baisse de 20 % des crédits PAC. Parce que l'Ukraine, bien évidemment, prendrait un très gros morceau de la PAC. Alors, nous savions que, pour l'Union européenne, l'agriculture n'était plus une priorité. Nous découvrons maintenant que l'Union européenne veut faire mourir l'agriculture européenne.

paragraphs.text: Monsieur le Président, chers collègues, alors que Poutine bombarde les cathédrales de Kiev, on enterre l'avion de chasse franco-allemand. Alors que s'envole le prix de l'énergie, nos usines de batteries et de panneaux solaires ferment faute d'investissements européens. Et voilà que Trump bloque notre accès aux IA les plus puissantes. L'Europe est prise dans la tourmente de ses dépendances économiques. Le Parlement a proposé une réponse budgétaire à la hauteur en faisant de la défense du spatial, du digital, des clean tech de nouvelles priorités, sans sacrifier les politiques de solidarité.

Et que font les États membres? Ils pinaillent. Chacun fait ses additions et tous proposent des soustractions. Mais quelle misère! Le Conseil européen doit cesser ses calculs de boutiquiers. Le prochain sommet européen doit mettre sur la table des négociations la seule discussion qui permettra de sortir de l'impasse, celle sur les nouvelles ressources propres pour financer ces investissements vitaux. Il y va de l'avenir de l'Europe comme continent libre et prospère.

paragraphs.text: Herr Präsident, sehr geehrter Herr Kommissar! Auf dem kommenden Gipfel müssen wir uns dringend mit den grundlegenden Sachen beschäftigen, und die grundlegenden Sachen sind, dass die Europäische Union wieder wettbewerbsfähig ist. Ich habe jetzt von vielen hier heute ständige Beschwerden über Drittstaaten gehört: Unsere Aufgabe als Europäisches Parlament ist es doch nicht, uns über Drittstaaten zu beschweren, sondern unsere Aufgaben zu lösen.

Im vergangenen Mandat – 2019 bis 2024 – haben die Kommission, das Parlament und der Rat erhebliche Fehler gemacht, die unserer Wettbewerbsfähigkeit geschadet haben. Das haben sie eingesehen – der richtige Weg. Einsicht ist der richtige Weg. Wir müssen jetzt wettbewerbsfähig werden.

Und wie das geht? Das haben wir doch unter Corona bewiesen: Die ganze Welt hat nach einem Impfstoff gesucht, und Europa hat ihn entdeckt. Wir sind die, die Innovation treiben können. Wir sind die, die mit Leidenschaft die Probleme der Welt lösen können, und das geht nur, wenn wir ein level playing field mit China haben und wenn wir uns gegen die Subventionen in China schützen.
Und das müssen Sie verstehen: Wenn wir unsere Kraft entfesseln, dann sind wir wettbewerbsfähig. Wenn Sie weitermachen mit Ihrer Planwirtschaft, gehen wir unter.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, Commissioner, Minister, colleagues, the West fundamentally misunderstood China. China pursues a simple but effective strategy – dictatorship at home and coercion, deception and protectionism abroad.

We were blind, believing that economic liberalisation would lead to political freedom. Instead, China used its WTO accession to perfect a pattern of dominance, dependency and blackmail designed to drive out competitors.

China's economic model is built on protectionism, massive state subsidies, massive theft of intellectual property, and currency manipulation aimed at dominating strategic industries such as, for example, now electric vehicles – not to save the planet, but to gain economic and geopolitical leverage.
With mounting internal problems, China will double down on export-driven growth targeting Europe. We need to react to that decisively.

China's economic model is built on protectionism, massive state subsidies, massive theft of intellectual property, and currency manipulation aimed at dominating strategic industries such as, for example, now electric vehicles – not to save the planet, but to gain economic and geopolitical leverage.

With mounting internal problems, China will double down on export-driven growth targeting Europe. We need to react to that decisively.

paragraphs.text: Voorzitter, het beschermen van onze burgers moet de absolute prioriteit zijn, daar is zowat iedereen het over eens. De voorbije vijf jaar zijn onze defensiebudgetten in Europa verdubbeld van 200 miljard naar 400 miljard. Gigantisch. Dat is het goede nieuws. Het slechte nieuws is: we staan eigenlijk nergens met een Europese pijler binnen de NAVO en we staan ook bijna nergens met de uitvoering van artikel 42, lid 7, van het Verdrag. Daar moeten we werk van maken.

Mijnheer de commissaris, ik begrijp dat de Europese Raad zich zal buigen over de implementatie van dat artikel. Wel, ik doe een suggestie: maak, zoals met het Verdrag van Schengen, een apart verdrag, een apart defensieverdrag. Laat de coalitie van bereidwillige landen daaraan meewerken en betrek daar ook Oekraïne, Noorwegen en het Verenigd Koninkrijk bij. En laat ons met de coalitie van bereidwillige landen vooruitgaan. Als we echt vinden dat het beschermen van onze burgers een prioriteit is, dan moeten we daar nu werk van maken.

paragraphs.text: Senhor Presidente, Senhor Comissário, o senhor comissário pede‑nos unidade. Unidade em quê? A um acordo em que ficamos bem pior do que estávamos antes da guerra? Bater palmas, talvez ao BCE, que decidiu subir as taxas de juro, agravando a crise do custo de vida na Europa?

A Comissão Europeia pede‑nos unidade contra os povos que devemos defender. Tenha vergonha, Senhor Comissário, e Senhora Ministra, a sério que Israel continua fora da agenda do Conselho? Sabemos agora que a Comissão escondeu durante dez anos, quase dez anos, um parecer jurídico para acabar com o Acordo de Associação. O Conselho vai continuar a tocar a mesma música, agora em modo de banda de Titanic?

paragraphs.text: Señor presidente, señor comisario, un mercado único, una defensa única y reglas únicas, no hay otro camino. Pero necesitamos ir más rápido y más lejos. Debemos liderar, no gestionar la decadencia. O lo logramos ya o, como advirtió Draghi, la agonía será lenta y dolorosa.

Debemos avanzar en tres direcciones. Primera: la económica, acelerando el mercado único, abriendo autopistas al talento, a la inversión, a la innovación, para reequilibrar la balanza global. No es solo comercio, es poder y geopolítica.

Segunda: la seguridad. La Unión Europea de Defensa no es una opción ideológica, es supervivencia. Ucrania está demostrando que Rusia puede ser derrotada, pero Putin será más peligroso cuanto más débil se sienta. Y Rumanía es la alarma que algunos siguen sin escuchar. Debemos seguir aprendiendo de Kiev y avanzar en su europeización.

Y tercera: la coherencia. Si la Unión Europea quiere ser respetada fuera, debe hacerse respetar dentro. España, la cuarta economía, es un país arrasado por la corrupción que deambula sin presupuestos desde hace tres años, incumple los compromisos de defensa, pisotea los dictámenes sobre el Estado de Derecho, hace negocios con enemigos que comprometen nuestra seguridad y desafía a Bruselas con una regularización masiva y legal, justo cuando aprobamos el Pacto sobre Migración y Asilo. Ante eso, la Comisión no puede permanecer callada porque millones de españoles se preguntan qué más tiene que ocurrir. ¿Acaso la Comisión no ha aprendido las lecciones de la Hungría de Orbán?
Señores de la Comisión, sin autoridad política no hay confianza ciudadana. Y sin confianza seguiremos...

paragraphs.text: Voorzitter, ik ben een beetje verbaasd door de centrale boodschap van de Europese Volkspartij vandaag. Het is niet de eerste keer: door het goedkeuren van het akkoord met de Verenigde Staten gisteren, gaan we nu lekker een team maken met de Verenigde Staten om een strategie te ontwikkelen naar China toe. Dat lijkt me alvast een heel dom idee. Ik denk dat we vooral vanuit onze eigen sterkte moeten vertrekken als we een strategie maken rond China. En die is duidelijk heel erg nodig. Dat spreekt voor zich, want China heeft een strategie. We kennen die: heel exportgericht, erop gericht om de sleuteltechnologieën van onze industrie over te nemen, zodanig dat wij ze zelf kwijtraken, en er daarbij voor zorgen dat onze industrie eronderdoor gaat. En dat betekent heel slecht nieuws voor heel veel werknemers.

We hebben dus een duidelijke strategie nodig: handelsbescherming, de verordening industriële versnelling en heel hard werken aan onze eigen soevereiniteit. Ik denk dat het heel belangrijk is dat er op heel korte termijn een overcapaciteitsmechanisme wordt ontwikkeld. Commissaris, ik denk dat we weten wat die strategie moet zijn.

paragraphs.text: Monsieur le Président, chers collègues, Monsieur le Commissaire, l'année dernière, pour la première fois, tous les pays européens ont enregistré un déficit commercial avec la Chine, même l'Allemagne. Pour la première fois l'année dernière, nous avons importé plus de voitures chinoises, plus de machines-outils chinoises que nous avons exporté de voitures européennes et de machines-outils européennes et notamment allemandes. Cela veut dire que plus aucune économie européenne, y compris l'Allemagne, n'est à l'abri du tsunami chinois qui est en train d'arriver et qui est en train de détruire les bases de notre tissu industriel.

Nous devons donc nous protéger et nous devons investir dans l'innovation, parce que, si les Chinois aujourd'hui gagnent des parts de marché, c'est certes parce qu'ils sont subventionnés, certes parce qu'ils ont des pratiques déloyales, mais aussi, reconnaissons-le, parce qu'ils ont investi plus que nous ne l'avons fait ces dernières années. Et donc nous devons gagner ces deux batailles, la bataille de l'investissement et la bataille du level playing field, la bataille de la protection. Et je crois que les choses changent beaucoup en Allemagne aujourd'hui, ce qui nous permet – et je souhaite que la Commission soit offensive sur ce sujet – ce qui nous permet...

paragraphs.text: Domnule președinte, fac parte din delegația cu China și am asistat la foarte multe întâlniri și la foarte multe discuții. Cred că nu ați înțeles că în acest moment China deține cea mai înaltă putere și este cea mai mare forță economică a lumii. Mai mult, face parte din BRICS, BRICS care are 49 % din produsul intern brut la nivel internațional.

Dumneavoastră, în loc să colaborați și să dialogați și să aveți o diplomație cu China, de câte ori au fost întâlniri, nu ați făcut altceva decât să întrebați de Taiwan, ceea ce înseamnă lipsă totală de respect față de statul chinez și o lipsă totală de diplomație. Dacă ar fi să ne gândim la câte Taiwan-uri sunt în lumea aceasta, s-ar putea să nu mai avem o Europă unită niciodată. Ar fi bine să vă intereseze doar relațiile Uniunii Europene cu China, nu să vă implicați în treburile interne ale unui stat care nu sunt problema voastră.
Mai mult decât atât, dumneavoastră refuzați dialogul, în timp ce toate celelalte țări au afaceri cu China. Îi acuzați degeaba, pentru că, din păcate, Uniunea Europeană a căzut.

paragraphs.text: Signor Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, intanto in bocca al lupo ai capi di Stato e di governo che saranno chiamati a trovare soluzioni nel prossimo Consiglio europeo. In bocca al lupo perché oggi, al di là di tanti slogan, di soluzioni concrete purtroppo ne abbiamo sentite poche.

Mi ha colpito l'ennesimo siparietto tra socialisti e popolari. In particolar modo, non mi aspettavo che i socialisti – va bene che siamo sotto mondiali di calcio – si travestissero da atleti di Cristo e citassero addirittura il Papa e ci parlassero di dignità umana. Quindi, se questa è la maggioranza che regge questo Parlamento, tanti auguri.

A proposito, il regolamento rimpatri: so che non vi piace, ma dovete farvene una ragione perché finalmente, anche se non è un testo perfetto, potrebbe rappresentare il primo tassello per passare da un'immigrazione quantitativa a un'immigrazione più qualitativa.
Le persone sono in difficoltà in questa fase. Abbiamo bisogno di un Parlamento che lavori, che trovi soluzioni concrete e meno siparietti.

paragraphs.text: Sehr geehrter Herr Präsident, Herr Kommissar, liebe Kolleginnen und Kollegen! Die politische Rhetorik wird robuster, wenn man politisch nicht handeln kann oder will.

paragraphs.text: Senhor Presidente, Senhor Comissário, caros colegas, o debate sobre a China é demasiadas vezes reduzido a falsas escolhas: cooperação ou confronto, abertura ou proteção, diálogo ou firmeza. Mas a Europa não tem de ficar condicionada a estes pares. Precisa de uma estratégia que os torne compatíveis.

A China é a principal origem das nossas importações e o terceiro maior destino das nossas exportações. Por isso, sim, temos de aprofundar o diálogo. Mas não o podemos fazer a partir de uma posição vulnerável. E sabemos bem o quanto a indústria europeia depende de cadeias de valor que passam pela China. Ainda assim, a dependência não existe só de um lado. A China precisa do acesso ao nosso mercado e, por isso, temos de conseguir usar melhor o peso da nossa economia para conseguir reciprocidade para as empresas europeias.

Mas esse peso só conta se falarmos a uma só voz. Quando cada um dos nossos Estados‑Membros visita Pequim em busca de acordos bilaterais, a China ouve 27 vozes, mas nenhuma com força suficiente para se impor e ser respeitada. A força da Europa não está na soma dos nossos países, está na nossa união.

Permitam‑me que termine com uma palavra dirigida aos nossos parceiros chineses: a Europa não procura o confronto, procura uma relação justa. Mas uma relação assim não se constrói sob pressão, constrói‑se com confiança. Essa confiança tem de ser mútua. Não se exige, conquista‑se com respeito, reciprocidade e regras claras.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, Iratxe García Pérez has unfortunately left us, but her speech reminded me a little bit about the story of this driver on the motorway who listens to the radio and hears a warning about another car dangerously driving in the wrong direction, and this driver looks around and says, 'One? I see loads of them.' And this is the story of the socialists today. Spain was the only country that voted against the return regulations. Three socialist leaders were in favour of it. More than 20 of your own colleagues supported it. So maybe it's time to consider also that they might not be the crazy ones here. And thank you also to the socialists for invoking the Pope and Christianity. You should do it more often is what I recommend to you, but do it less selectively, perhaps. Invoking the Pope when it politically suits you while ignoring him on everything else is not faith; it's hypocrisy.

President, three small points on the summit this week. First, on Ukraine, it's crucially important that we support Ukraine. But also here we see that it's a small number of Member States that are doing most of the supporting, while others – like Spain, again – contribute little to nothing. This is unacceptable and cannot continue.
Second, on defence, there is still a gap between our strategic ambition and our operational delivery and that gap must be closed.

And third, on drugs, we need action against third countries that harbour drug traffickers. Criminals like Bolle Jos in the Netherlands should not be able to escape justice simply by finding protection abroad in a country like Sierra Leone. We need to prepare to use all our leverage.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, let us be honest about who we are dealing with. When China wants its leverage, it weaponised rare earths, choking the supply of materials that our industries, our defence and our green transition depend on. When we moved to reform our cybersecurity, Beijing threatened our businesses. The pattern is always the same – cooperation is offered when we are useful and pressure is applied the moment we act in our own interest.

We keep answering this with dialogue; they answer with coercion. A partner who only respects strength will keep pushing until they meet some, so we should make their divide and conquer tactics carry a real cost. We should impose tariffs where China dumps and distorts, we should make access to our markets strictly reciprocal, and we should pursue China through the WTO when it breaks the rules and deindustrialises the European Union in the process.

paragraphs.text: Monsieur le Président, chers collègues, nous nous apprêtons à adopter un règlement historique qui permettra d'expulser beaucoup plus efficacement les clandestins, fruit d'une coalition des droites qui a mis en minorité la majorité d'Ursula von der Leyen. C'est une grande satisfaction, mais nous ne devons pas nous contenter de lutter contre l'immigration illégale. Le prochain chantier qui doit nous occuper est la jugulation de l'immigration légale cette fois, alors que nous connaissons une augmentation record de la population immigrée en Europe.

Celle-ci représente 64,2 millions de personnes, soit presque autant que la France métropolitaine. Et en 2024, l'Union européenne a délivré 3,5 millions de premiers titres de séjour à des ressortissants de pays tiers. Le Conseil a donc le devoir: un, de mettre fin aux multiples pompes aspirantes comme le regroupement familial, deux, réduire le périmètre du droit d'asile, trois, supprimer les trop nombreuses exemptions de visas. Il doit faire pression sur le gouvernement espagnol, qui prend l'ensemble de l'espace Schengen en otage en régularisant massivement des étrangers clandestins. Voilà des sujets qu'il nous faut urgemment mettre à l'ordre du jour du prochain Conseil européen.

Et donc je vous invite éventuellement à vous pencher sur le sujet et à poser la question la prochaine fois à Jordan Bardella.

paragraphs.text: Domnule președinte, împărtășesc și salut entuziasmul din jurul noilor negocieri de aderare și felicit președinția cipriotă pentru succesul deschiderii primului cluster pentru Moldova și Ucraina, dar e important să nu ne autoamăgim doar cu mesaje de felicitare pe social media. Extinderea este crucială pentru securitatea și relevanța Uniunii Europene, însă ea nu trebuie doar susținută la nivel declarativ, ci trebuie accelerată urgent prin măsuri concrete.

Timpul nu mai este de partea noastră, iar întârzierile ne fac vulnerabili. Dincolo de promisiuni politice, este nevoie de resurse reale. Realitatea este că fără un viitor cadru financiar multianual, adecvat și gândit special și pentru procesul de extindere, nu putem construi o Europă mai mare și mai unită, cu bugete diminuate.

De aceea, astăzi am un mesaj clar: cer liderilor de state și guverne să treacă la o viziune curajoasă și asumată pe termen lung, bazată pe recunoașterea meritelor și performanțelor individuale. Renunțați la perspectiva limitată, dictată doar de calculele unui singur ciclu electoral. Istoria nu așteaptă după următoarele runde de alegeri. Viitorul Europei trebuie...

paragraphs.text: Signor Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, è inutile girarci intorno. Il prossimo Consiglio sarà l'ennesimo fallimento, come tutti quelli che lo hanno preceduto. Fallimento sulla pace: zero diplomazia, armi e guerra infinita in Ucraina. Fallimento sull'economia: prezzi dell'energia alle stelle, zero investimenti e nessun piano di sostegno per famiglie ed imprese.

Nel nuovo mondo multipolare, l'Europa dovrebbe dialogare con tutti, essere perno tra Est e Ovest. E invece trattiamo la Cina e i paesi BRICS come nemici per compiacere gli Stati Uniti, che cercano lo scontro per fermare il loro declino.

Ma guardiamo in faccia la realtà. Trump vi ha umiliati sui dazi, costretti a sostituire il gas russo con il GNL statunitense, che costa di più ed è più impattante per l'ambiente. Ci stanno spingendo dritti alla recessione. Trattare Pechino come rivale strategico, mentre siete letteralmente genuflessi dinanzi al governo genocida di Israele, è un suicidio politico.

L'Europa non ha bisogno di nemici, né di sostituire vecchi padroni con i nuovi padroni. I cittadini europei hanno bisogno di una classe dirigente che faccia i loro interessi. Esattamente ciò che non fate e non state facendo voi.

paragraphs.text: Herr Präsident, meine sehr geehrten Damen und Herren! Im deutschen Sprachgebrauch gibt es eine Formulierung, die da lautet: Sind Sie denn des Wahnsinns knusprige Beute? Das mag ich der EU entgegenrufen, wenn vor zwei Tagen das erste Beitrittskapitel mit der Ukraine für einen EU-Beitritt eröffnet wurde.

Die Ukraine ist ein im Krieg befindliches Land. Die Ukraine geht unter in Korruption – ich sage nur Stichwörter: vergoldete Toilettenanlagen, in Plastik eingeschweißte Millionen von Dollar- und Euroscheinen. Die Ukraine hat seit Jahren keine Wahlen mehr durchgeführt und sich demokratisch legitimiert. Die EU macht mit diesem Schritt eine Überdehnung ihrer eigenen Fähigkeiten und richtet sich noch mehr zugrunde, als sie es ohnehin schon selbst tut.

Ja, die Ukraine soll mittel- und langfristig die Option für eine Partnerschaft für Handel haben – überhaupt keine Frage. Aber jetzt hier in Vorbereitung der Ratssitzung die Ukraine hereinzuholen in die Europäische Union, ist ein No-Go und soll und darf nicht passieren.

paragraphs.text: Señora presidenta, señorías, la paz, la dignidad humana y el respeto al Derecho internacional deben ser los ejes centrales de los debates y conclusiones del Consejo Europeo.

Queremos la paz en Ucrania y en Oriente Medio. Pero el camino hacia la paz no se decidirá sin Ucrania y tampoco sin la Unión Europea, que está prestando apoyo holístico e inquebrantable con medidas financieras como el préstamo de 90 000 millones de euros.

Igualmente, la Unión debe jugar un papel activo para el final de la guerra ilegal y absurda desatada por Trump y Netanyahu en Irán y en el Líbano. Debemos mantenernos firmes porque, de lo contrario, la paz que se firmó hace solo tres días quedará en papel mojado.

Queremos respeto a la dignidad humana en Gaza y Cisjordania, empezando con una condena enérgica a la pena de muerte israelí para los palestinos y continuando con el apoyo a la asistencia humanitaria y la reconstrucción de una región devastada. Solo así caminaremos hacia la solución de dos Estados, el único camino hacia la paz duradera en esa región.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, let me just react on three points on the Council agenda.

First of all, on Russian aggression. Ukraine is showing strength on the battlefield every day, but it would not be possible without continuation of our economic, political and military support. We must keep going, not only because it's the right thing, but, as it was said by our chairman, our relationship with Ukraine is not a liability. It is an asset for us and we must act accordingly.

The second, on enlargement, just keeping going with what we were doing so far is not enough. We must conclude negotiations with some Balkan countries that are prepared for membership and work out a plan to develop quickly a much stronger relationship with others that, for strategic reasons, need to join.

Last but not least, on competitiveness: One Europe, One Market is a great plan, but we must deliver – deliver not only on small things, but especially on large things like the electricity market, banking union and so on. But, at the same time, leaders should understand that it's up to them to improve the market by removing the obstacles that were created on the Member State level. Unless we do it, this agenda will not be complete and will not deliver.

paragraphs.text: Frau Präsidentin, Herr Kommissar, liebe Kolleginnen und Kollegen! Stellen Sie sich vor, Sie verlieren jeden Tag eine Milliarde EUR und Ihr einziger Plan ist es, den Verbrennungsmotor noch fester zu umarmen: Willkommen in Europas China-Politik. Denn genau das passiert – jeden Tag kaufen wir für eine Milliarde EUR mehr in China ein als China bei uns; während ich hier rede, ist also die nächste Milliarde schon auf dem Weg.

Alle Länder der Europäischen Union exportieren inzwischen mehr in die Schweiz als nach China – also 8 Millionen Eidgenossen schlagen 1,4 Milliarden Chinesen. Und was ist das Ergebnis? Wir verlieren in Europa jeden einzelnen Tag tausend Industriejobs.

Und dann sagen manche: Schuld ist die Klimapolitik. Die Welt baut Zukunft, und Sie suchen einen Sündenbock. Nennen Sie mich konservativ: Ich will, dass wir in Europa von der Industrie noch etwas übrig haben. Es ist nicht konservativ, im Museum zu wohnen. Das ist keine Politik; das ist Nostalgie mit Insolvenzgarantie. Den Chinaschock haben wir jetzt verschlafen; wachen wir auf, denn wer nicht in die Zukunft investiert, verliert.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, Commissioner and colleagues, I just want to talk about the debate we've been having about China. I was on the trade committee in the last mandate, and we put an awful lot of effort into developing a whole raft of trade defence instruments around anti-dumping, FDI screening, the procurement instrument and anti‑coercion, among a range of other things. And we appointed a chief trade enforcement officer. And yet here we are today. And it strikes me that all of these measures that we put so much effort into are not being effective. We introduced tariffs on EV subsidies from China, and in Q1 2026, we saw an 82 % increase in imports of EVs from China over Q1 of 2025.

So I think what we need to do is, yes, we're doing great on trade agreements. It's brilliant to have an agreement with India, with Mexico, with Australia. But on our trade defence instruments, we need to resurface the assumptions around these instruments. We need possibly to have an omnibus on this to make sure that they are actually effective, because they haven't been effective in the last few years.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, what's the definition of madness? Doing the same thing over and over again and expecting a different result. According to that logic, the European Council is insane. Every time a wannabe dictator is finally voted out, another one pops up. And so we're held hostage by 27 national elections and national vetoes.

The Council is kind of like the Greek myth of Sisyphus, who pushes a boulder up a hill, but every time he's near the top, it rolls back down, repeating for eternity. Seizing frozen Russian assets: almost there – veto! Making the European elections more democratic: almost there – veto! Abolishing the veto – veto!

This Friday, Volt protests in front of the Council to demand national leaders do what most Europeans want: abolish the veto and unite. We will do this over and over again until we push that boulder over the top.

Sabemos que debemos fomentar una relación comercial estable y mutuamente beneficiosa, pero el mismo Lao Tse también recomendaba afrontar los problemas antes de que ocurran y poner las cosas en orden antes de que haya confusión.

Es innegable que existen importantes desórdenes y desequilibrios en nuestras relaciones económicas: la sobrecapacidad industrial, las subvenciones estatales sin precedentes, las dependencias críticas que ponen en riesgo nuestra industria y una falta de reciprocidad que lastra a nuestras empresas en el exterior. paragraphs.text: Madam President, I want to talk about two points on your agenda: Ukraine and defence. They are connected by a lack of sense of urgency, I am sorry to say, in particular with the Member States.

There are many good things in the draft conclusions, and you will say to me: 'Yes, look what we are doing'. But condemnations of Russia's attacks don't save lives. Air defence, deep strike capability and integrated air protection zone do save lives. So how many heads of state and government have been called by von der Leyen, Kallas and Costa in the past ten days? Because we have sent letters about it, we have called for them to send these air defence systems to Ukraine.

The second point on defence; there is also no lack of good words in the conclusions, but where is the sense of urgency? Member States continue to spend money with nationalist reflexes. No internal market on defence, no collective procurement, wasting tens of billions – tens of billions! – per year. I want now a sense of urgency. The Member States are holding us back out of fear for what? 27 capitals are endangering our security.
