interventions.speaker_label: Pascal Canfin, au nom du groupe Renew.

paragraphs.text: Monsieur le Président, chers collègues, aujourd'hui, nous avons la possibilité de donner de nouveaux outils à nos agriculteurs et le groupe Renew soutient ces nouveaux outils, comme nous avons soutenu les solutions basées sur la nature. Car contrairement à d'autres ici, nous n'opposons pas les solutions écologiques et les solutions technologiques. Parce qu'en fait, les agriculteurs ont besoin des deux. La réalité est que nous devons leur donner tous les outils dont ils peuvent disposer pour lutter contre le dérèglement climatique, s'adapter, réduire les pesticides chimiques et gérer le stress hydrique.

Aujourd'hui, les nouvelles techniques génomiques leur donnent cette nouvelle possibilité. C'est centré là-dessus. Nous avons créé un modèle européen et le Parlement a considérablement amélioré la proposition initiale de la Commission européenne en créant un modèle européen des nouvelles techniques génomiques. Il ne s'agit pas, contrairement à ce que disent certains, d'importer le modèle américain, d'importer le modèle brésilien des nouvelles techniques génomiques, mais au contraire de créer un modèle souverain de nouvelles techniques génomiques qui servira nos agriculteurs, leurs revenus, nos rendements et notre souveraineté alimentaire.

interventions.speaker_label: Martin Häusling, im Namen der Verts/ALE-Fraktion.

paragraphs.text: Herr Präsident, liebe Kolleginnen und Kollegen! Das Trilog-Ergebnis verstößt ganz eindeutig gegen das, was wir hier im Parlament wollten, nämlich keine Patente auf Saatgut; da haben wir eine ganz klare Mehrheit gehabt. Jetzt sollen sie plötzlich kommen. Das gefährdet den europäischen Saatgutsektor, das gefährdet die Rechte der Züchter, und wir machen das Tor ganz weit auf für amerikanische, chinesische Gentech-Konzerne. Wollen wir das wirklich? Ich glaube, das können wir nicht akzeptieren.
Zweitens wollte das Parlament Transparenz, eine Wahlfreiheit der Verbraucher: Ganz klar sollte am Ende Gentechnik gekennzeichnet werden. Auch das wurde nicht erreicht.

Drittens sage ich, wir schmeißen damit unser Vorsorgeprinzip über den Haufen. Keine Rückverfolgbarkeit, keine Risikoprüfung – das können wir einfach nicht akzeptieren. Es ist nach wie vor eine Risikotechnologie.
Und was ich auch noch einmal betone: Alle Pflanzen können patentiert werden; es gibt keine Grenze.

Ich finde dieses Ergebnis des Trilogs nicht akzeptabel. Liebe Kolleginnen und Kollegen, lassen Sie uns bitte noch einmal darüber diskutieren! Akzeptieren Sie diejenigen, die Änderungsanträge eingebracht haben!

interventions.speaker_label: Anja Hazekamp, on behalf of The Left Group.
interventions.speaker_role_in_transcript: on behalf of The Left Group

paragraphs.text: Mr President, this legislation undermines the very foundations of our food system. This is not by accident. This is deliberate.

This law is a direct result of the aggressive lobbying by the big agro-biotech companies. They hope to increase their already-obscene profits, as they can patent these new GMOs. This gives the multinationals even more power over our food system at the expense of farmers and citizens.

Right now, we can still guarantee the genes of organic products haven't been tampered with. But if you vote for this law, we cannot guarantee that anymore, because the labelling requirements and traceability of these GMOs will be removed. GMOs will soon be on our plates without risk assessment and without being able to say no.
Colleagues, don't let the industry intimidate you. Don't let the group leaders intimidate you. Vote with your heart. Vote with common sense. Vote against this law.

interventions.speaker_label: Anja Arndt, im Namen der ESN-Fraktion.

paragraphs.text: Herr Präsident, sehr geehrte Abgeordnete! Heute geht es nicht um Fortschritt oder Stillstand. Heute geht es um das Vertrauen, Wahlfreiheit und Kontrolle über unser Saatgut, unsere Lebensmittel und unsere Landwirtschaft.

Wir stimmen über die Deregulierung sogenannter NGT1-Pflanzen ab. Diese Pflanzen werden mit neuen genomischen Techniken genetisch verändert und können in Lebensmitteln, Futtermitteln und auf unseren Äckern landen. Uns wird gesagt, das könne theoretisch auch natürlich oder durch konventionelle Züchtung entstehen, aber Theorie ersetzt keine praktische Erfahrung, und Geschwindigkeit ersetzt keine Sicherheit.
Wer solche Technologien in die Breite bringt, muss Kontrolle, Transparenz und Wahlfreiheit garantieren. Doch genau das fehlt, weil die Kennzeichnungspflicht fehlt.
Es gibt auch kein rechtssicheres Patentverbot. Damit werden NGT1-Pflanzen zum Einfallstor für Biopatente, Konzernmacht, Monopole und neue Abhängigkeiten unserer Landwirte und Züchter.

Solange Kennzeichnung, Rückverfolgbarkeit und ein wirksames Patentverbot fehlen, darf es keine Zustimmung zur Ratsposition geben. Ich empfehle deshalb die Zustimmung zu allen Änderungsanträgen, die die Kennzeichnungspflicht einfordern und die Patentierbarkeit ausschließen, und am Anfang der Ablehnung der Linken und Grünen zuzustimmen.

paragraphs.text: – Before the vote:

interventions.text: – Before the vote:

paragraphs.text: Κύριε Πρόεδρε, αγαπητοί συνάδελφοι, η αποτελεσματικότερη καταπολέμηση της διασυνοριακής απάτης στον ΦΠΑ είναι ζωτικής σημασίας. Είναι ένα οικονομικό έγκλημα που στερεί δεκάδες δισεκατομμύρια ευρώ από τα ευρωπαϊκά και εθνικά ταμεία. Προκαλεί τεράστια απώλεια δημοσίων εσόδων, στρέβλωση του υγιούς ανταγωνισμού και επιβάρυνση των έντιμων φορολογούμενων. Έχουμε απώλειες δισεκατομμυρίων ευρώ, τα οποία θα μπορούσαμε να αξιοποιήσουμε για την υγεία, την παιδεία, τη στέγαση και την καινοτομία.

Η αποτελεσματική και χωρίς καθυστερήσεις συνεργασία μεταξύ του Eurofisc, της Ευρωπαϊκής Εισαγγελίας και της Ευρωπαϊκής Υπηρεσίας Καταπολέμησης της Απάτης είναι επιβεβλημένη. Οι σχετικές πρόνοιες περιλαμβάνουν την κεντρική πρόσβαση στις αναγκαίες πληροφορίες ΦΠΑ και πλήρη σεβασμό στους κανόνες προστασίας προσωπικών δεδομένων.

Ευχαριστώ θερμά το Ευρωπαϊκό Λαϊκό Κόμμα που με εμπιστεύτηκε να είμαι ο συντάκτης της έκθεσης, και όλους τους συναδέλφους από όλες τις πολιτικές ομάδες για την εποικοδομητική συνεργασία. Σας ευχαριστώ και σας καλώ να υπερψηφίσετε την έκθεσή μου.

paragraphs.text: – Before the vote:

interventions.text: – Before the vote:

paragraphs.text: Signor Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, il Parlamento è chiamato a esprimere una posizione tanto inedita – è la prima volta – quanto attuale, sulla governance dell'acqua, nella prospettiva di garantire pace, rule of law e human rights.

Ben 150 bacini idrici sovrastatali costituiscono nel mondo un'occasione di collaborazione ma anche di conflitti in riferimento all'acqua definita "bene comune pubblico". Guerre che usano l'acqua come armi. Migrazioni che trovano motivazione forte nella mancanza di acqua. Speculazioni che mortificano il diritto all'acqua e costituiscono un pretesto per violazione del rule of law. Sono tutti argomenti trattati con un testo di compromesso per il quale sento il dovere di esprimere apprezzamento agli shadow dei diversi gruppi e agli staff della commissione per gli affari esteri e degli stessi rapporteur.
L'auspicio è l'approvazione di una determinazione che costituisca conferma di importanza dell'acqua e della sua governance per una pacifica convivenza tra i popoli.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, colleagues, maybe before you go, you can give me your attention for one final moment. I think what happened here today is more a matter of Rule 10(3).

But I just want to tell you something before you leave. Now, after you leave, this Chamber will be empty again, just as it was this morning, just as it was yesterday, just as it will be tomorrow. Because this Chamber is empty. And when we are full, when this Chamber is full, and we have a topic that moves us, then this Chamber acts like a circus. Then we have colleagues who chant at each other, who scream at each other, instead of having a debate.
I think this is a disgrace, and I think the European Parliament is better than that. So maybe we can take this as an opportunity to at least apply the plenary reforms that were implemented ...

paragraphs.text: Mr President, I just wanted to say that I have never felt as unsafe in this Parliament as after the vote about the Return Regulation, because the shouting of the far right was not against the political opponent, it was 'send them back'. It was about ordinary people who did no other crime than looking for a better life in Europe, and shouting about ordinary people who are not present in the room, it is a new, new low level even for the fascists on the far right.

And I hope that you, as Chair of the sessions, also take care about our safety here in the Chamber and stop that kind of behaviour, because that is far beyond what racism is, far beyond what hatred is against ordinary people who have not done anything but come here to Europe to seek for a better life. We can have a political debate, we can argue against it ...

paragraphs.text: Mr Chair, Mr Commissioner, Council representative. 2026, beginning of 2026. And I will switch to my mother tongue.

2026 metų pradžioje per Lietuvoje veikiančią įstaigą Registrų centras, kuri atsakinga už šalies gyventojų ir juridinių asmenų duomenų registrą, buvo pavogta virš šešių šimtų tūkstančių Lietuvos gyventojų svarbių asmeninių duomenų, įskaitant žmonių asmens kodus, adresus, turimo nekilnojamo turto įrašus. Lietuvos teisėsaugos duomenimis, neteisėti prisijungimai prie Registrų centro duomenų bazės vykdyti per iš užsienio pasisavintas šalies Migracijos departamento darbuotojų paskyras.

Generalinė prokuratūra tęsia tyrimą pagal tris Baudžiamojo kodekso straipsnius. Tyrimas jau išplėstas ir siekiama atsakyti ir į klausimus, ar visos šalies institucijos tinkamai atliko pareigas ir ėmėsi visų priemonių informacijai ir duomenims apsaugoti. Lietuvos valdžios institucijos daugiau nei šešiems šimtams tūkstančių gyventojų, kurių duomenys buvo pavogti, nepagrįstai ilgai vėlavo pranešti apie įvykdytą neteisėtą jų duomenų pasisavinimą. Nors pirmieji neteisėti prisijungimai ir duomenų vagystės įvykdytos dar šių metų pradžioje, o Registrų centrui ir atskirų valstybių Lietuvos ministerijų vadovams didžiulė vagystės apimtis tapo žinoma dar balandžio pradžioje, po keturių mėnesių, visuomenei apie incidentą pranešta tiktai daugiau nei po pusantro mėnesio, gegužės pabaigoje. Klausimai, kodėl paaiškėjus faktams atsakingos institucijos, įskaitant Lietuvos Vyriausybės vadovus, vengė apie tai informuoti nukentėjusius gyventojus, iki šiol lieka neatsakyti.

Norėčiau pabrėžti: būtų naivu remtis prielaida, kad išaugusios geopolitinės grėsmės ir padidėjęs kibernetinių atakų skaičius yra tiktai Lietuvos problema. Užtikrinti kibernetinį saugumą šių dienų augančių grėsmių akivaizdoje iššūkis visai Europos Sąjungai, neaplenkiant nė vienos valstybės ar institucijos.

Prieš Lietuvą atakos toliau tęsiasi. Vien per pastarąsias savaites Lietuvoje pranešta ir apie kibernetinį incidentą, per kurį, kaip įtariama, pasisavinta kone 62 000 įrašų apie Lietuvos medikus. Taip pat viešumą pasiekė informacija apie galimai pusšimtį nulaužtų Lietuvos Vidaus reikalų ministerijos sistemos paskyrų. Priešiškos jėgos surinktą informaciją, kuri yra pavogta prieš tai, žinoma, gali vėliau panaudoti sekant, spaudžiant ir bauginant žmones, įskaitant svarbias pareigas einančius asmenis.

Todėl šiandien reikia naujų kibernetinio saugumo standartų ir, žinoma, pilno jų įgyvendinimo. Remiantis prielaida, kad NIS2 direktyva, Europos Sąjungos Bendrųjų duomenų apsaugos reglamentas, nustatantis privalomus kibernetinio saugumo standartus, galioja jau nuo 2024 metų, bet direktyvos įgyvendinimas lieka skylėtas. Pavyzdžiui, Vokietijoje iki 2026 metų kovo mėnesio tik apie trečdalis organizacijų, privalančių registruotis pagal NIS2 reikalavimus, buvo tai padariusios. Taisyklės, kurios neįgyvendinamos, neapsaugo nieko, jos neveikia.

Europos Komisija privalo atlikti pilną tyrimą dėl Lietuvoje įvykusios duomenų vagystės, nustatant priežastis ir atsakingus už įvykusį nusikaltimą asmenis. Europos duomenų apsaugos reglamento įgyvendinimas reikalingas pilno patikimumo visos Europos Sąjungos mastu. Kitaip mūsų duomenys tampa blogos valios ir nusikaltėlių medžiaga, kuri gali būti vėliau panaudota prieš mus pačius. Ačiū už jūsų dėmesį.

paragraphs.text: Now we will move to the Council and we have the Deputy Minister for European Affairs, Marilena Raouna. I would also like to thank the Cypriot Presidency for its work. This is your last plenary, so thank you so much.

interventions.text: Now we will move to the Council and we have the Deputy Minister for European Affairs, Marilena Raouna. I would also like to thank the Cypriot Presidency for its work. This is your last plenary, so thank you so much.

political_group.label: S&D
political_group.name: Group of the Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats in the European Parliament

interventions.speaker_label: Marilena Raouna, President-in-Office of the Council.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, Honourable Members, Commissioner, it is clear that the rapidly increasing number of serious and sophisticated cyberattacks is greatly concerning for our citizens and for our industries. In today's environment of hybrid threats and escalating cybercrime, Member States stand stronger together. That is precisely why we have built a strong and coordinated system to reinforce our cybersecurity as a core pillar of our democracies, but also of the resilience of the single market. We have, in recent years, developed a solid legislative cyber framework, and we are working to strengthen it further.

In this context, we welcome the Commission proposal for a new cybersecurity package, which is currently under discussion in the Council. The Council supports a strengthened role for ENISA, the EU Agency for Cybersecurity, to support operational cooperation in enhancing cyber resilience at the EU level and also amongst Member States. We all recognise that today's security environment is not only defined by cyberattacks, but by broader hybrid threats from malign actors. These threats are increasingly sophisticated, combining cyber operations, foreign information manipulation and interference, economic coercion, sabotage and other tactics. While the primary responsibility for cyber security and countering hybrid threats remains with the Member States as a matter of national security, the Council has developed a comprehensive framework for a coordinated EU response to hybrid campaigns, as well as the EU Cyber Diplomacy Toolbox to increase the EU's ability to prevent, discourage, deter and respond to malicious cyber activity. This includes Hybrid Rapid Response Teams, which can be deployed upon request to support the Member States and partner countries in countering hybrid threats.

The framework is supported by the External Action Service, which provides a centralised analytical capacity to detect and assess hybrid activity. In March, the Council adopted conclusions on advancing the EU's capacity to counter hybrid threats, reaffirming our determination to use all available tools. Also, the European Democracy Shield, together with the European Centre for Democratic Resilience, further reinforces our collective efforts. The challenge is to move from a reactive approach to anticipation and prevention. Let me assure you that the EU is constantly strengthening its ability to support Member States in detecting, deterring and disrupting hybrid campaigns before they can fully materialise. Thank you for your attention.

interventions.speaker_label: Michael McGrath, Member of the Commission.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, dear Deputy Minister, dear honourable Members, today the threats we face are not isolated incidents, but coordinated waves of hybrid attacks aimed at weakening the very fabric of our democracies. This is why cases such as the Lithuanian case of the data breach that you put on the agenda of the Plenary today must be treated with the utmost seriousness.

While the specifics of the Lithuanian case would need to be addressed by the competent authorities, the scale of such a breach can generate distrust in the ability of democratic authorities and frameworks to safeguard the fundamental rights of our citizens.

The only durable and effective way forward against threats and challenges like these is to take a whole of government, a whole of society, and a whole of cycle approach to protect our collective democracies.

As part of this approach, the Commission adopted the European Democracy Shield in November of last year to strengthen and to protect our democracies. Its actions complement the broader EU work to counter hybrid threats.

In particular, we have now set up the European Centre for Democratic Resilience as a hub for strategic and practical cooperation between EU Member States and EU institutions and bodies, supporting the sharing of information, best practices and capacity-building. It can also serve as a nexus for facilitating practical cooperation and enabling the Member States to develop common response options when faced with similar challenges.

When we talk about hybrid threats, a key component is indeed cybersecurity. The NIS2 Directive ensures that our essential services know what measures to take in order to work on preventing cyber incidents.

Additionally, once it enters into application next year, the Cyber Resilience Act will make sure digital products are secure all across the EU. In addition, the Cyber Solidarity Act establishes a European Cybersecurity Reserve, a pool of trusted experts who can be called upon to support any country that may be in need.

We should also make use of the EU hybrid toolbox and its associated cyber diplomacy and FIMI toolboxes, which give us the means to identify those responsible for malicious hybrid activities and to respond through coordinated diplomatic action.
We have also proposed a revision of the Cybersecurity Act to strengthen the mandate of ENISA, equip it with the right resources, and to address risks across ICT supply chains.

Democratic resilience also depends on the enforcement of rules in reality, including the application of the General Data Protection Regulation. The GDPR places clear obligations on controllers to secure personal data through appropriate technical and organisational measures, and to notify national data protection authorities and affected individuals when breaches pose a high risk. Enforcement is then a matter for national authorities, who must investigate and follow up accordingly.
I look forward to hearing your contributions to today's debate and indeed to responding to them.

paragraphs.text: Gerbiamas Pirmininke, kolegos. Hibridinių grėsmių spektras, kurį patiria Europa, o kaip atskiras atvejis – ir Lietuva, yra įspūdingas. Dezinformacijos kampanijos, migracijos instrumentalizavimas, kontrabandinių balionų, klajoklių dronų nukreipimas – štai tas, bet dar nepilnas sąrašas. Prie viso to, Lietuvoje neseniai įvykdyta duomenų vagystė iš Registrų centro, tyliai nukopijuojant daugiau negu šešis šimtus tūkstančių nekilnojamojo turto ir juridinių asmenų registro įrašų. Tad kibernetinė infrastruktūra vis dažniau tampa prioritetiniu taikiniu – ir tikrai ne vienintelėje Lietuvoje, būta panašių atvejų ir Europos Sąjungos institucijose, o žala sunkiai išmatuojama. Pavogti duomenys virsta priešų žvalgybos ištekliais. Iš skaičių ir įrašų susidėlioja tikslūs profiliai – atveriamos teisėjų, diplomatų, karių ar pilietinės visuomenės atstovų privačios gyvenimo erdvės. Asmeniui iškyla tiesioginės grėsmės, o valstybei daroma dar ir reputacinė žala.

Incidentas atskleidė struktūrinę problemą – teisės normos ir techninės priemonės nespėja paskui grėsmes. Šiuolaikinės kibernetinės operacijos veikia lyg šešėlis: jos yra decentralizuotos, pasklidusios per dešimtis serverių įvairiose jurisdikcijose, sunkiai lokalizuojamos ir dar sunkiau priskiriamos konkrečiam vykdytojui, o tada atsiranda nebaudžiamumas. Skaitmeniniai pėdsakai greit išnyksta arba tyčia sunaikinami, o tyrėjams atstatyti nuoseklų įvykių vaizdą tampa sudėtinga arba neįmanoma. Todėl atsakas turi būti proporcingai greitas, kaip ir pati ataka. Tyrėjai turi turėti ne tik teisinius įgaliojimus, bet ir realias technines priemones veikti nedelsiant. Europos Sąjunga privalo veikti kaip vieninga gynybinė erdvė, o tas veikimas koordinuojamas, bet ne prikuriant biurokratinių derinimo mechanizmų, o priešingai – didinant tyrimo tempą. Dėkoju.

political_group.label: PPE
political_group.name: Group of the European People's Party (Christian Democrats)

interventions.speaker_label: Vytenis Povilas Andriukaitis, on behalf of the S&D Group.
interventions.speaker_role_in_transcript: on behalf of the S&D Group

paragraphs.text: Mr President, Commissioner, colleagues, protecting European Union citizens' data from hybrid threats is of paramount importance in this digital age. When data is compromised, citizens lose confidence not only in their governments, but in the very system designed to serve them. Unfortunately, Lithuanians have experienced exactly this during a recent breach of the national Register Centre. Although authorities said that no crucial personal data was stolen, IT services fixed the gap and started criminal investigation without delay. This was one of the reasons why the information was not conveyed to the public immediately.

In this episode, a broader vulnerability is illustrated. The incident exposes the limits of relying solely on individual Member States' interpretations and protocols when it comes to the security of critical digital infrastructure. I believe there is a clear need for more stringent European‑level guidelines, both on the security standards required to such an end and on how authorities should communicate.

interventions.speaker_label: Julie Rechagneux, au nom du groupe PfE.

paragraphs.text: Monsieur le Président, en France, nous faisons face à une offensive permanente et systémique contre nos données. Le constat est accablant: nous sommes aujourd’hui le deuxième pays le plus touché au monde par les violations de données. Les données de 43 millions de personnes ont été dérobées chez France Travail; 2 millions de dossiers de l’Office français de l’immigration se sont retrouvés en vente sur le «dark web»; le fichier national des comptes bancaires de la DGFiP a été consulté pendant seize jours… Dans notre pays, le casse du siècle, c’est tous les jours.

Derrière les données volées, il n’y a pas seulement des risques financiers, il y a aussi des victimes en chair et en os: des dirigeants d’entreprises, des investisseurs qui sont ciblés par des enlèvements et des séquestrations de plus en plus violents. Les données sont devenues le nouvel or du XXIe siècle. Alors, sommes-nous vraiment prêts, comme certains le veulent dans ce Parlement, à affaiblir la définition même de données personnelles?

Depuis vingt ans, l’Europe s’est imposée comme la référence mondiale en matière de protection des données. Mais protéger les données, c’est bâtir des systèmes résistants aux attaques, c’est empêcher que des millions de données sensibles ne se retrouvent exposées à la première faille. C’est le grand enjeu de notre siècle, et nous ne pouvons pas nous permettre de rater la marche.

Monsieur le Président, en France, nous faisons face à une offensive permanente et systémique contre nos données. Le constat est accablant: nous sommes aujourd’hui le deuxième pays le plus touché au monde par les violations de données. Les données de 43 millions de personnes ont été dérobées chez France Travail; 2 millions de dossiers de l’Office français de l’immigration se sont retrouvés en vente sur le «dark web»; le fichier national des comptes bancaires de la DGFiP a été consulté pendant seize jours… Dans notre pays, le casse du siècle, c’est tous les jours.

paragraphs.text: Gerbiamas Pirmininke, kolegos. Sovietmečiu buvo mada rašyti laiškus ir skųstis Maskvai. Mados nepasikeitė, pasikeitė tik adresatai. Noriu jums kai ką pacituoti: „Programuotojai per kelis mėnesius pateikė informacijos ne tik apie tam tikras nutekintos informacijos atkarpas, bet apie visą sistemą, kaip tai, kur informacija laikoma. Duomenų bazėse kaupiama medžiaga iš Lietuvos institucijų, ministerijų, savivaldybių, taip pat privačių asmenų informacija, taip pat vienos iš šalies politinių partijų serverių duomenys. Mes kalbame apie juodąjį internetą, kuriame tikrai labai daug informacijos.“ Citatos pabaiga.

Ši informacija buvo paskelbta Lietuvos Parlamente 2024 metų kovo pradžioje. Tuomet ministerijai vadovavo šiuo metu taip aktyviai Lietuvos problemomis Europoje besiskundžiančių parlamentarų kolegė, nekreipusi jokio dėmesio į įspėjimus apie pavojus. Ar tuomet taip pat buvo siūloma diskusija Parlamente? Ar buvo informuota Europos Komisija? Kodėl duomenų saugumas parūpo tik šiandien? Augant ambicijoms skaitmenizuoti paslaugų teikimą, vis daugiau duomenų kaupiama įvairiose valstybės duomenų sistemose. Tai tampa ne tik privalumu ir patogumu, bet ir didžiuliu iššūkiu institucijoms, iššūkiu gyventojams, kurie praranda pasitikėjimą valstybės gebėjimu užtikrinti duomenų apsaugą, ir, galų gale, iššūkiu politikos sprendimų priėmėjams, nes tikėtina, kad visuomenė nepasitikės skaitmenizacija. Todėl tai yra visų mūsų reikalas, ne tik tų, kurie, turėję galimybę pasirūpinti duomenimis, šiandien užsiima pigiu politikavimu.

paragraphs.text: Gerbiamas Pirmininke, gerbiamas komisare, gerbiami kolegos. Europos Sąjungos valstybių registruose saugoma vis daugiau jautrios informacijos, todėl šiandien duomenų apsauga yra visų pirma nacionalinio bei europinio saugumo klausimas. Duomenų vagystės neabejotinai domina Rusijos ir kitų Europai priešiškų šalių žvalgybas. Joms svarbu rinkti žvalgybinę informaciją apie mūsų politikus, pareigūnus, pilietinės visuomenės lyderius, identifikuoti jų pažeidžiamas vietas, kad galėtų smogti jiems agresijos ar hibridinių grėsmių atveju. Būtent todėl tai, kas nutiko Lietuvoje, nėra vien tiktai vidaus reikalas, negali būti vertinama tik kaip vienos valstybės vidaus politikos problema. Nuo mūsų reakcijos į šį incidentą priklausys tai, kaip panašios hibridinės operacijos bus vertinamos ateityje. Jeigu tokie atvejai nebus nuodugniai ištirti, o kibernetinio saugumo spragos nebus pašalintos, siųsime pavojingą signalą, kad tai galima kartoti ir kitose Europos Sąjungos valstybėse.

Šis incidentas kelia klausimų ir dėl Europos Sąjungos teisės laikymosi. Nors Lietuvos institucijos apie gyventojų duomenų vagystę žinojo bent jau nuo balandžio, visuomenė buvo informuota tik gegužės pabaigoje. Priminsiu, kad Bendrojo duomenų apsaugos reglamento 34-asis straipsnis numato pareigą nedelsiant informuoti gyventojus apie asmens duomenų saugumo pažeidimą, kai tai gali kelti didelę riziką jų teisėms ir laisvėms. Todėl kviečiu Europos Komisiją aktyviai įsitraukti ir paprašyti Lietuvos institucijų pateikti išsamius paaiškinimus: ar buvo visapusiškai ištirti visi šio incidento aspektai, įskaitant priešiškos žvalgybinės veiklos dimensiją? Ar buvo imtasi visų būtinų priemonių apsaugoti piliečių duomenis?

Ši krizė ir pačioje Lietuvoje turi tapti lūžio tašku. Jos nebus įmanoma išspręsti vien keičiant vadovus ar skiriant daugiau finansavimo. Būtina iš esmės pertvarkyti valstybės informacinių technologijų politiką. Lietuvos atvejis turi tapti pamoka ir visai Europos Sąjungai.

paragraphs.text: Gerbiamas Pirmininke. Taip, gerbiami Europos Parlamento nariai, tikrai labai įdomu, kada tas skundimas, jau ne pirmą kartą iš Lietuvos pusės, savo šalies vyksta iš liberalų ir konservatorių. Lietuvos nacionalinio kibernetinio saugumo centras prie Krašto apsaugos ministerijos dar 2022 metais patvirtino rekomendacijas dėl Registrų kibernetinio centro saugumo. Jis pasiūlė dvigubą identifikaciją, bet to nepadarė ir inovacijų tuometinė ministrė, Žalimo, kuris ką tik kalbėjo, partijos pirmininkė, ir jis ją skundžia. Žinoma, reikia pripažinti, kad to nepadarė ir dabartinis ministras. Gerbiamieji, aš manau, kad patys turime susitvarkyti su savo problemomis ir neskųsti čia į Briuselį, nes esate labiausiai kalti liberalai.

paragraphs.text: Gerbiamas Pirmininke, gerbiami kolegos. Na, iššūkiai egzistuoja ir dažnai, kai mes kalbame apie nacionalinį saugumą, mes pirmiausia įsivaizduojame tą tokį tradicinį: oro gynyba, tankai, tvoros, sienos, bet hibridinės grėsmės, kurias patiria Baltijos šalys, kurios pirmiausia kyla iš Rusijos, Baltarusijos, jos yra įvairių formų ir viena iš jų yra, be jokios abejonės, susijusi su mūsų piliečių duomenų apsauga. Todėl kibernetinis saugumas yra ne ką mažiau svarbus ir investicijos į kibernetinį saugumą yra ne ką mažiau svarbios nei į tradicinę gynybą, ypatingai į mūsų piliečių duomenis.

Mes matome, kad ilgą laiką tiesiog ignoravome tą ir ignoravome tą visoje Europoje. Šiandieninis pavyzdys, kas įvyko Lietuvoje su nutekinimu Registrų centro duomenų, parodė, kad tie įstatymai, kurie galioja, jie negali pakankamai apsaugoti mūsų piliečių. Todėl ne tik įstatymai reikalingi, bet reikalingos ir konkrečios iniciatyvos ir investicijos, kurios užtikrins ir nacionalinį saugumą, bet taip pat ir užtikrins mūsų piliečių saugumą. Todėl Komisijai labai svarbu yra ne tik teikti iniciatyvas, bet matyti vaizdą ir konkrečiai padėti valstybėms narėms apsaugoti piliečių duomenis.

interventions.speaker_label: Michael McGrath, Member of the Commission.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, I thank the representatives of the political groups for those initial contributions to this debate, and I thank you for putting the interests of the citizen at the heart of this debate, because EU citizens have a right to have their personal data protected. And when that right is not respected or when it is breached, we know it can have far-reaching ramifications in terms of their trust and confidence in public institutions, and indeed in the very democratic system itself. Many of you have called for a united response, you have called for a coordinated response, both at a national and also at an EU level, and I believe that that is what we are doing, and we need to review how we can step up and strengthen our efforts in working together.

In relation to the framework of the new European Centre for Democratic Resilience, we are taking a number of steps. We are developing a capacity-building project rooted in the train-the-trainer logic. We are bringing together the Member State expertise under the French stewardship to ensure coherence by defining common concepts and methodologies for detecting FIMI. We will make sure that we boost our capabilities of preventing and detecting threats, providing Member States with the right tools and solutions. For example, the Nordic-Baltic Cyber Hub will support early detection of such threats and enhance cross-border cooperation between partners.

Let me also use the opportunity to highlight that in two weeks' time, in line with the ProtectEU Strategy, we will propose a strengthening of the mandate of both Eurojust and Europol, which will improve their capacity to support national authorities in countering criminal threats, including where they have a hybrid dimension. Deterring cyberattacks requires also that our national authorities have better tools and support so that they identify or attribute attacks to those behind them and can effectively prosecute and sanction them. We need to have digital evidence and effective tools, building on the roadmap for lawful and effective access to data for law enforcement also.

Finally, to conclude, Mr President, hybrid threats, FIMI and cyberattacks are designed to exploit the fragmentation that a number of you have highlighted here already this afternoon. So, therefore, we must work together, and I take that as the key message away with me so far in the debate – to collectively build our defence in the interests of national security, in the interests of European security, but also in the interests of upholding the fundamental rights of EU citizens, including the right to have their personal data fully protected.

paragraphs.text: Panie Przewodniczący! Jako sprawozdawca Parlamentu Europejskiego do spraw mobilności wojskowej w Komisji Bezpieczeństwa i Obrony jestem przekonany, że bezpieczeństwo Europy zależy nie tylko od naszych zdolności obronnych, od infrastruktury transportowej, od szybkości działań, ale również od bezpieczeństwa naszych sieci, systemów informatycznych i danych obywateli.

To kwestia bardzo ważna i ten przypadek Litwy pokazuje, że bezpieczeństwo cyfrowe jest dziś nierozerwalnie związane z bezpieczeństwem europejskim. Już we wtorek podczas posiedzenia dwóch komisji przyjmiemy pakiet ustawodawczy „Mobilność wojskowa”. Mam nadzieję, że na kolejnym posiedzeniu Parlamentu otrzymamy zgodę do przeprowadzenia negocjacji międzyinstytucjonalnych.

Ale również ta dyskusja o działaniach hybrydowych Rosji musi spotkać się z nowymi informacjami, które mamy z Polski. 15 czerwca w Polsce został zastrzelony Siemion Skierpiecki. To jest artysta, performer, który był bardzo krytyczny wobec reżimu Putina. Stało się to w Białej Podlaskiej, a trzy dni wcześniej ten artysta był w Berlinie i protestował przed ambasadą rosyjską. To pokazuje, że Rosja eskaluje swoje działania poza granicami, również w Unii Europejskiej. Musimy w tej sprawie być jednością.

paragraphs.text: Gerbiamas Pirmininke, komisare, kolegos. Gyvename laikais, kai kibernetinės atakos tapo neatsiejama vykdomo hibridinio karo prieš Europą dalimi. Pastaraisiais mėnesiais matėme dronų incidentus prie Europos Sąjungos ir NATO rytinio flango sienų, provokacijas Baltijos jūroje prieš kritinę infrastruktūrą, dezinformacijos kampanijas. Šie išpuoliai ir veiksmai nėra atsitiktiniai. Jų tikslas – silpninti mūsų saugumą, kurstyti nepasitikėjimą ir testuoti Europos atsparumą. Todėl kiekvieną duomenų nutekinimo atvejį turime vertinti ne vien tik kaip privatumo pažeidimą, bet ir kaip nacionalinio bei Europos saugumo klausimą.

Taip, įvykęs duomenų nutekinimas Lietuvoje kelia pagrįstą visuomenės susirūpinimą. Todėl būtent todėl turime stiprinti valstybės informacinių sistemų saugumą, investuoti į kibernetinę gynybą, diegti pažangias prieigos kontrolės priemones ir užtikrinti nuolatinį kritinių sistemų auditą. Suprantu opozicijos norą ieškoti politinės atsakomybės, tačiau šiandien svarbiausia ne politiniai kaltinimai, o sprendimai, kurie sustiprins piliečių duomenų apsaugą ir Lietuvoje, ir visoje Europos Sąjungoje. Ačiū.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, the recent data breach in Lithuania, involving more than 600 000 records from national registers is a stark, grim reminder that hybrid threats are no longer directed only at governments or critical infrastructure. They target our citizens directly. Investigators suspect foreign involvement, highlighting the growing use of cyber operations as a tool of hostile influence and destabilisation.

When personal data are stolen, citizens become vulnerable to espionage, intimidation, disinformation, and identity theft. Protecting data is therefore not only a matter of privacy, it is a matter of national and European security.

The European Union must strengthen cyber resilience, improve information sharing among Member States and fully implement our cybersecurity and data protection frameworks. Lithuania's experience should serve as a warning to us all: an attack on the data of one Member State is an attack on the security of the entire European Union. We must be prepared.

Vedem datorii de trilioane pentru război, Green Deal și vaccinuri inutile. Ne mințiți că economia verde a Uniunii Europene este competitivă. Vedem doar falimente, concedieri, sărăcie, poluare crescândă.

Ne mințiți că ne apărați libertatea, dar ce vedem este lipsirea de libertate și derapajul antidemocratic. Ne mințiți că Ucraina va fi victorioasă, cu condiția să continuăm fluviul de bani către regimul său corupt. Vedem însă doar incidente cu drone ucrainene care pun în pericol orașe întregi ale României și zeci de tone de bani cash, tranzitând liber România către Ucraina.
O minciună repetată la infinit nu devine adevăr, iar fapt este că voi sunteți adevărata amenințare hibridă de care cetățeanul european trebuie protejat.

paragraphs.text: Herr Präsident, sehr geehrter Herr Kommissar! Erst heute hat mir jemand in den sozialen Medien geschrieben: Ich soll nicht übertreiben, es gibt doch keinen hybriden Krieg gegen Europa und gegen europäische Länder. Hier haben wir aber den Beweis: Ja, es gibt ihn. In diesem Fall hat es eben 600 000 Einträge aus dem Melderegister von Litauen betroffen. Es kann jederzeit auch uns in Österreich treffen – jeden von uns, mit allen Folgen. Und ja, wir wissen, es sind die Russen. Was wollen die Russen? Putin ist es. Was will er machen? Er will Europa zerstören, er will uns Angst machen und möglicherweise auch erpressen.

Die Antwort darauf kann nur technologische Unabhängigkeit sein; da müssen wir noch viel stärker werden – wir haben ja auch gestern schon darüber gesprochen – und natürlich die Sicherheit ausbauen. Und ja, Herr Kommissar, völlig richtig: Eurojust und Europol müssen zusammenarbeiten, auch mit den nationalen Institutionen.

Dazu kommt aber noch etwas; ich glaube auch, weil es ja um Desinformation geht, worüber wir auch schon oft gesprochen haben, was ja auch ein Teil dieser hybriden Angriffe ist, neben Cyberangriffen, neben Sabotageakten; da müssen wir eben auch dieses Resilience Centre gemeinsam ausbauen. Ich glaube, es spricht wirklich sehr viel dafür, ein starkes europäisches EU-Resilience Centre zu haben, das mit den nationalen Regierungen zusammenarbeitet und mit dem auch wir als die gewählten Mandatarinnen und Mandatare Europas zusammenarbeiten.

Und wir müssen das Bewusstsein schaffen – wie gesagt, viele Leute verstehen noch gar nicht, wie vielfältig die Angriffe laufen: nicht nur militärisch, brutal gegen die Ukraine, sondern durch hybriden Krieg auch gegen uns.
Wehren wir uns! Wie so oft: Es geht nur gemeinsam – wir als starkes Europa.

paragraphs.text: Herr Präsident, liebe Kolleginnen, liebe Kollegen! Angesichts dieser Debatte erlauben Sie mir mal, Donald Trump, den amerikanischen Präsidenten, zu zitieren, der mal gesagt hatte: Die größte Bedrohung für unsere Demokratie kommt nicht aus Russland oder aus China; die größte Bedrohung kommt von innen.
(unverständlicher Zwischenruf eines anderen Abgeordneten)
Genau, Herr Sieper.
Und in diesem Fall ist die größte Bedrohung für die Datensicherheit und für die Meinungsfreiheit der europäischen Bürger die Europäische Kommission und hier vor allem das Digital Services Act.

Hier wird, unter dem Vorwand des Kinderschutzes, versucht, jegliche Systemkritik zu unterdrücken und eine totale Kontrolle zu etablieren. Ein ähnliches System wurde bereits in Australien unter dem gleichen Vorwand eingeführt, und alle Daten zeigen, dass es nicht funktioniert; über 60 % der Minderjährigen haben nach wie vor Zugang zu sozialen Medien.
Also hier geht es im vollsten Wissen um etwas anderes: Hier wird versucht, eine Ausweispflicht einzuführen. Das ist eine Sozialkontrolle wie in China, das ist das Ende der Meinungsfreiheit in der EU.

paragraphs.text: Senhor Presidente, Senhor Comissário, caros colegas, a Lituânia, como se percebe, tem estado na linha da frente desta nova forma de agressão, destes ataques híbridos que têm uma estratégia sistemática de agressão ao nosso espaço europeu e de agressão às nossas democracias.

A Lituânia tem enfrentado tentativas de intimidação, de desestabilização, destinadas a explorar as vulnerabilidades das nossas sociedades, e o objetivo parece‑nos claro: que se semeie o medo, se criem divisões e se dissemine a confiança dos cidadãos nas instituições democráticas.

É por isso, Senhor Comissário, que, ao longo destes tempos, temos analisado esta questão na nossa Comissão Especial sobre o Escudo Europeu da Democracia. Voltando a reforçar o que o nosso colega do Grupo Renew referiu: é muito importante que o Centro Europeu da Resiliência Democrática exista com competências próprias, com a participação de todos os Estados e com a capacidade não apenas de reagir a estas ameaças mas também de garantir a prevenção, que é absolutamente essencial para que a desinformação não se propague e para que as nossas democracias não continuem ameaçadas.

paragraphs.text: Signor Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, innanzitutto solidarietà alla Lituania per quello che è accaduto.

Il tema dei dati, dei dati sensibili, del controllo, della possibilità di gestire il tema della sicurezza attraverso i dati ci riguarda tutti. Non c'è un confine fisico quando parliamo di dati. Questo è uno degli argomenti che stiamo trattando anche nella discussione dello Space Act europeo, ma dobbiamo interrogarci anche sulle catene di approvvigionamento che poi gestiscono i sistemi del controllo dei dati.

Oggi ogni chip proviene dalla Cina. Potrebbe essere una potenziale capacità di cattura di informazioni. Lo sappiamo attraverso la gestione dei dati sulla mobilità. Lo sappiamo quando trattiamo di dati sensibili sulla sanità.
Dovremmo interrogarci su come rendere indipendente l'Europa in una lunga filiera che vede il controllo dei dati come minaccia finale, ma che deve essere costruita fin dalla sua progettazione.

E con questo dobbiamo anche permettere alle forze di polizia e alle forze dell'ordine di essere più libere di gestire. Troppe volte le contraddizioni tra privacy e dati diventano una forma di incapacità di difesa.

paragraphs.text: Panie Przewodniczący! Litwa – można powiedzieć mały kraj, ale wielki przykład dla nas wszystkich. Na Litwie w wyniku cyberataku wyciekły dane setek tysięcy obywateli. Za tą operacją – wiele na to wskazuje – stały rosyjskie służby wywiadowcze zainteresowane pozyskaniem wrażliwych informacji o państwie członkowskim Unii Europejskiej. To problem Litwy, ale i Polski, i całej Europy. Kiedy atakowane są rejestry publiczne jednego państwa członkowskiego, atakowana jest wspólna przestrzeń bezpieczeństwa Unii Europejskiej.

Litwa od lat pokazuje Europie, jak przeciwstawiać się rosyjskiej dezinformacji i agresji. Dziś zasługuje nie tylko na naszą solidarność, ale także na konkretne działania. Potrzebujemy wyższych standardów cyberbezpieczeństwa, szybszego informowania obywateli o zagrożeniach oraz zdecydowanej odpowiedzi na wszelkie wrogie operacje. Bo suwerenność w XXI wieku to nie tylko obrona terytorium, to także bezpieczeństwo naszych danych, naszych instytucji i naszych obywateli.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, Commissioner, dear colleagues, when hostile actors target a national register, they are not merely stealing data, they are targeting trust in our state institutions.

This is why the recent breach of Lithuania's centre of registers is so alarming. More than 600 000 records were unlawfully accessed, including personal identification data, addresses and property information. Among those affected may be public officials or members of the security services, whose data could be exploited by hostile intelligence services.

Investigation could lead to foreign state involvement. This would not be a technical incident. It would be another hybrid attack. Cyber threats do not stop at national borders, and neither should our ability to prevent, detect and respond to them. We need coordinated European cyber defence architecture.

The EU has already taken important steps to strengthen our collective cybersecurity. Through NIS2, we are raising security standards for critical sectors and public administration across Europe. Through the Cyber Solidarity Act, we are improving our ability to detect threats early, share intelligence and support Member States. Agencies, such as ENISA, together with national cybersecurity authorities, are helping to build a stronger and more coordinated European response.
So, dear colleagues, more single market for cybersecurity as well.

paragraphs.text: Señor presidente, señor comisario McGrath, miembros del Consejo, yo vengo hoy aquí a solidarizarme con el pueblo lituano por el ciberataque que han tenido, pero sobre todo por elevar la voz en algo que me parece extraordinariamente importante: Europa está fuera de juego en este momento en materia de ciberseguridad. No tiene un centro único de respuesta. Yo creo que deberíamos desarrollar un centro único de respuesta propio, netamente europeo.

La Unión no tiene un sistema de inteligencia netamente europeo. Rusia sí. Rusia tiene el GRU, tiene un sistema militar donde para cada ciberataque, junto con operaciones militares, va de una forma única.

También hay una cuestión que yo vengo reivindicando en los últimos tiempos y que me preocupa de una forma muy especial: la conjunción de la nueva inteligencia artificial de carácter ofensivo —no voy a hablar de Anthropic y de Mythos—, pero es que China también tiene su propio desarrollo y Rusia también tiene su propio desarrollo. ¿Cuál es la respuesta de la Unión Europea ante esto?

Eso, unido también al nuevo desarrollo de la computación cuántica, nos puede dejar prácticamente en un año fuera de juego. Esto es algo muy grave que tanto el Consejo como la Comisión tienen que abordar de forma inmediata.

paragraphs.text: Herr talman! "Tror du verkligen på riktigt att Ryssland skulle attackera Sverige?" Det är en fråga jag får nu och då, men svaret är ju glasklart: Ryssland har länge och uttalat hotat hela Europa och vår demokrati. Ryssland menade allvar med Krim och blodigt allvar med Ukraina. Ryssland söker ständigt efter våra sårbarheter, med sabotage, drönare och attacker på digitala system.

Vårt ansvar – vårt gemensamma europeiska ansvar – är att se till att Ryssland inte får möjlighet att förverkliga sina hot och ambitioner. EU och våra myndigheter måste kraftsamla för att sätta stopp för dessa hot.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, Commissioner, colleagues, Lithuania is a success story. Lithuania, if you didn't yet know, is, according to analysis, the state with the happiest youth on earth. Lithuania is an EU Member State that was in history part of the so‑called Soviet Union. Now Lithuania has been attacked – like many parts of Europe – via hybrid means and measures, and among them is cyberattacks.

600 000 – a vast number of data of persons has been stolen by Putin's Russia. This is a huge number given the size of the country. We must not underestimate what that means in terms of interference, especially in the country that is a success story also in terms of digitalisation, of using digital means and measures to preserve not only bureaucracy but also democracy, confidence and trust within a society.

A text like that must not remain uncommented by us. This is why it is important that the whole European Parliament is standing behind Lithuania. I thank my dear colleague Rasa Juknevičienė for raising the issue, for putting the issue in the centre of the very European Parliament, and for giving us the opportunity to ensure the Lithuanians of our full solidarity and of fighting back against these attacks from Putin's Russia.

I have heard broad convergence on the need to further strengthen our cybersecurity and our ability to respond to hybrid threats and to strengthen our cooperation. A lot has been done during the last few years, but we still have important work on the table. Strengthening our Union's resilience and capacity to address cyber and hybrid threats is a vital undertaking that will benefit us all.
The Council and the Member States will continue to work closely with the European Parliament and with the European Commission in this joint effort, in the interests of national and European security.

interventions.speaker_label: Michael McGrath, Member of the Commission.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, honourable Members, we need to transform Europe into the world's first electro-continent. At the moment, electricity accounts for just 23 % of Europe's energy consumption, and this figure has remained stagnant for years. While we have stayed put, other fossil fuel importers across the globe have been moving forward. For example, China and Japan are approaching an electrification rate of 30 % and beyond.

But now we have an opportunity to get back in the race, because in the midst of the current fossil fuel crisis, we are seeing the first sparks of an electrification revolution in Europe. While we welcome the agreement reached between the United States and Iran, we need to acknowledge once again our fossil fuel dependencies, and therefore we must progress swiftly with our electrification agenda if we want this fossil fuel crisis to be the last one.

According to the industry, more than 500 000 electric cars were registered across the EU in the first quarter of this year. That is enough to reduce our oil consumption by 2 million barrels per year. Meanwhile, in the same period, the combined sale of residential heat pumps in France, Germany and Poland surpassed 400 000 units, representing a 25 % increase compared to the first quarter of last year. Europeans are now reading the signs for sure – and they are choosing electricity. We need to follow their lead and we need to seize this momentum.

This is what we will aim to do in the Electrification Action Plan. The Commission plans to adopt an ambitious electrification target, and it will focus on supporting the sectors that are stalling the most. For industry, there is potential to expand the use of e‑boilers, heat pumps, electric drying technologies and small-scale electric furnaces. We also need to promote research and innovation to make new electrification solutions commercially viable for European industries.

Horizon Europe is supporting the development and upscaling of innovative technologies, including storage and renewable heating and cooling for transport. The benefits of electric vehicles are abundantly clear. Thanks to lower running costs and more affordable cars, EVs are now at a turning point in Europe, with battery electric vehicles becoming competitive with conventional vehicles over their time of ownership. To spread these benefits, we need to improve price transparency for EV charging, the deployment of vehicle-to-grid technologies, and corporate fleet strategies.

We also need to continue our efforts to drive electrification in buildings. The expansion of heat pumps, batteries and smart technologies offer game-changing possibilities. By installing these technologies across Europe, we can make a huge difference in the lives of millions of our citizens while scaling up EU manufacturing, creating high quality jobs and strengthening the resilience and sustainability of industrial energy supply.

But to deliver the full savings potential of electrification, we need to supply it with home-grown and affordable clean energy. This requires increasing domestic production of clean energy and a strong and interconnected European grid with the adequate storage and flexibility capacities. To proceed swiftly, we are helping Member States to speed up and to simplify permitting procedures for clean energy projects.

Beyond electrification, we can harvest efficiency gains in heating and cooling. This includes supporting the business case of clean heating, which is essential to complement electrification and make it efficient and affordable. Meanwhile, our clean energy investment strategy will help to de-risk projects and attract a wider base of investors with important support from the European Investment Bank. We should not forget that we will need electricity in abundance – also because of the rapid scale-up of data centres and artificial intelligence. With the strategic roadmap for digitalisation and AI, we outlined how we can best utilise AI for our energy system. The US export ban on Anthropic's latest AI model just last weekend also shows that the EU needs tech sovereignty and its own digital capacity.

Honourable Members, to conclude, Europe is at a pivotal moment for its independence and economic security. With the Electrification Action Plan, we will accelerate the energy transition and we will remove barriers to proceed with structural changes to become more energy independent. I look forward to your contributions this afternoon.

interventions.speaker_label: Raúl de la Hoz Quintano, en nombre del Grupo PPE.

paragraphs.text: Señor presidente, señor comisario, no cometamos los errores del pasado. La electrificación no es —ni puede ser nunca— un fin en sí mismo que haya que conseguir, estableciendo nuevas imposiciones a consumidores y a empresas.

La electrificación es una herramienta más para conseguir no solo descarbonizar nuestra economía, sino también reforzar nuestra competitividad. Y para conseguir estos dos objetivos, desde nuestro punto de vista, el plan de electrificación tiene que basarse en tres pilares.

El primero de ellos es la electricidad asequible. No puede ser que la electricidad que están pagando hoy nuestros consumidores y nuestras empresas sea dos y tres veces superior a la de nuestros competidores. Necesitamos abaratar el precio de la electricidad y ello exige invertir en redes, mejorar nuestras infraestructuras y nuestras conexiones, y también, por cierto, un mercado de la electricidad que incentive la producción asequible y limpia.

En segundo lugar, procedimientos más simples y mucho más rápidos. No puede ser que el desarrollo de infraestructuras energéticas en Europa se demore dos y tres años... nos está lastrando. Necesitamos procedimientos más ágiles, más rápidos, más simples y acelerados, sin condicionar en ningún caso con ello los estándares medioambientales.

Y, en tercer lugar, neutralidad tecnológica y soberanía energética. La electrificación requiere de una producción abundante, estable y asequible. Y ello no lo vamos a conseguir solamente con las energías renovables. Necesitamos incorporar la energía nuclear. No es una cuestión de ideologías, es una cuestión de realismo económico y energético.

En definitiva, para que el plan tenga éxito, desde nuestro punto de vista, debe enfocarse no solo en consumir más electricidad, sino en consumir electricidad de forma más eficiente, producida en Europa, a precios más asequibles.

political_group.label: PPE
political_group.name: Group of the European People's Party (Christian Democrats)

interventions.speaker_label: Mohammed Chahim, on behalf of the S&D Group.
interventions.speaker_role_in_transcript: on behalf of the S&D Group

paragraphs.text: Mr President, it's very simple. If we want energy security, if we want to lower our dependencies on foreign autocrats and if we want to keep industry in Europe, then the only one serious way forward is electrification.

We can continue spending billions of euros in fossil fuels and keep the dependencies – crisis, now crisis, now crisis – and I don't see any learning effect. Hundreds of billions that we spend and not a drop of gas or oil extra as Europe.

So we need to invest in technologies that make Europe stronger and more independent. That choice is today before us. European technologies like solar, wind and batteries are improving every year, or maybe even every month, and their price development goes in one direction: down. It becomes more affordable. That's why electrification is not only climate policy, it's industrial policy. It's security policy. It's economic common sense.

This is no longer a debate about the distant future. It's already happening. Families are installing heat pumps, drivers are switching to electric cars and companies are investing in cleaner production.

But too often they are told the grid cannot handle it. That's unacceptable. Sometimes the upfront costs are way too high. We need to help people with social-leasing schemes for heat pumps, for electric cars, etc. That's the way forward.
Electrification must lower emissions, strengthen Europe's independence and work for everyone: households, tenants, small businesses, workers and industry.

interventions.speaker_label: Paolo Borchia, a nome del gruppo PfE.

paragraphs.text: Signor Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, signor Commissario, sono diversi anni che sentiamo sempre gli stessi discorsi sull'elettrificazione. Come ha detto lei, siamo arrivati al 23 %: un aumento del 2 % in dieci anni. Allora, se la matematica non è un'opinione, ci chiediamo come facciamo ad arrivare entro il 2030 al 32 %. È tutta una guerra di percentuali che però ci fa capire quanto ci sia una strategia che è basata su poco.

Io parto dal presupposto che, se una soluzione è veramente convincente, c'è il mercato, ci sono i consumatori che poi si regolano in maniera quasi automatica. Le imprese tagliano i costi, le famiglie scelgono l'opzione più economica, senza bisogno di essere guidato o, peggio, senza che ci siano imposizioni dal punto di vista normativo.

Allora, se serve un piano costruito a tavolino, è perché nelle condizioni attuali l'elettrificazione evidentemente non è una soluzione sufficientemente convincente o economicamente conveniente. Questo io non credo sia un problema di ambizione, perché di target ambiziosi in quest'Aula ve ne siete inventati fin troppi. È un problema di distanza, un problema di distanza tra i costi che Bruxelles presuppone e i costi che la gente quotidianamente affronta. E fino a quando questa distanza resta, da Bruxelles si continuerà a cercare di vendere convinzione dove non esiste la convenienza.

paragraphs.text: Signor Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, signor Commissario, l'elettrificazione è diventata quasi un incubo oggi, perché tutti i target che ci siamo dati, scritti a tavolino in qualche oscura stanza della Commissione, non si raggiungono. Il 2030 è tra quattro anni, e tra quattro anni dovremo fare il 50 % in meno delle emissioni. Nel 2050 dovremo raggiungere la neutralità climatica.

Qui si disegnano dei progetti che non hanno nessun addentellato con la realtà. La realtà dice che, secondo il vostro disegno, si deve andare in direzione di: elettrificare l'industria, elettrificare i trasporti, elettrificare le case. Ma le reti? Quando ho fatto la domanda a un suo collega, ho chiesto: chi paga le reti? Con quali risorse paghiamo le reti che portano in questa ipotetica forma di poderosa elettrificazione? Con quali risorse? Non c'è stata alcuna risposta.
Ma la domanda è capziosa: chi sta guadagnando sull'elettrificazione? Cina. Allora chiediamoci se tutto questo qualcuno lo sta facendo non per l'Europa ma per un'altra nazione che non è questa.

Quando ho fatto la domanda a un suo collega, ho chiesto: chi paga le reti? Con quali risorse paghiamo le reti che portano in questa ipotetica forma di poderosa elettrificazione? Con quali risorse? Non c'è stata alcuna risposta.

Ma la domanda è capziosa: chi sta guadagnando sull'elettrificazione? Cina. Allora chiediamoci se tutto questo qualcuno lo sta facendo non per l'Europa ma per un'altra nazione che non è questa.

interventions.speaker_label: Christophe Grudler, au nom du groupe Renew.

paragraphs.text: Monsieur le Président, Monsieur le Commissaire, chers collègues, l'électrification est la clé de notre souveraineté énergétique. Mais nous n'allons pas assez vite, sur la demande notamment. Début 2026, l'Europe a connu plus de 1 200 heures de prix négatifs. Pendant plus de 1 200 heures, nous avons produit une électricité décarbonée sans pouvoir la vendre, faute de clients. Le vrai chantier, c'est donc la demande. C'est pourquoi le futur plan d'électrification doit être ambitieux et concret.

Cela passe par trois priorités. Fixer un objectif d'électrification. Développer la flexibilité de la demande et le stockage. Et enfin, mettre fin au mécanisme qui subventionne encore la production lorsque les prix deviennent négatifs. Enfin, il faut avoir le courage de réformer. Je pense à la directive sur la taxation de l'énergie bloquée depuis 20 ans. L'électricité décarbonée ne peut plus être davantage taxée que les énergies fossiles. L'électrification n'est pas une option. C'est une condition de notre compétitivité et de notre indépendance énergétique.

interventions.speaker_role_in_transcript: on behalf of the Verts/ALE Group

paragraphs.text: Mr President, Commissioner, dear colleagues, is the European Union trapped in a toxic relationship? You know the pattern: you give and you give, and you get nothing back. You become insecure, vulnerable, dependent on the other person's mood.

And let's be honest, that's exactly the relationship we Europeans have with oil and gas, dependent on the whims of autocrats like Putin and the mood swings of Donald Trump. We give and give – last year, EUR 420 billion for fossil fuel imports, almost EUR 1 000 per citizen, every single year. Money we burn and we wire abroad. And the dependency makes everything more expensive: energy prices, food, filling up the car, heating the home, until hardly anyone can afford to live anymore.

So what do you do with a relationship like this? Exactly: you break up. So let's break up with fossil fuels. But breaking up is not enough. We make ourselves stronger. And that is precisely what electrification is about. Europe has sun. Europe has wind. Let's build on our own strength. Every heat pump we install takes Putin's power over Europe away. Every wind turbine pays off with lower prices for heating, for driving, for living.
Electrification is not about renouncing. Electrification is about standing up for ourselves. Let's break up and finally start with ourselves.

paragraphs.text: Herr Präsident! Ja, meine Damen und Herren, wir haben hier heute auf der Tribüne auch Besucher aus Deutschland sitzen, und sie denken sich: Endlich mal hat es jemand kapiert, das Europäische Parlament, die Kommission reagiert – Electrification Action Plan –, es geht an meine Stromrechnung, endlich werden die Kosten gesenkt.

Nein, das ist nicht der Fall. Es wird wieder annahmeseitig auf der Nachfrageseite rumgearbeitet; es wird die Nachfrage nach Strom gesteigert. Das kann es nicht sein. Sie versprechen uns Jobs: Sie werden Jobs schaffen, aber in China. Wir haben 80 % der Wertschöpfung, was Solarzellen angeht, bekanntermaßen in China; wir haben keine großartige eigene Produktion.

Sie versprechen Wachstum: Sie werden Deindustrialisierung schaffen. Wir haben keine Netze, die dafür ausgelegt sind, diese Nachfrage handeln zu können; wir haben nicht die Batteriekapazitäten. Sie reden von einem Plan, der irgendwann in der Zukunft vielleicht umgesetzt werden könnte.
Aber das Hauptproblem, was ich daran habe, ist: Sie versprechen Freiheit durch beispielsweise BEV-Fahrzeuge und dergleichen mehr: Sie werden Unfreiheit und Planwirtschaft schaffen.
Das kann es nicht sein. Fortschritt entsteht durch Freiheit. Dieser Plan schafft keine Freiheit; er schafft Unfreiheit – und Ihnen keine günstigeren Preise.

interventions.speaker_label: Michael McGrath, Member of the Commission.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, I am delighted to have the opportunity to respond to the initial contributions in this debate from the representatives of the political groups.

Even in those early contributions, some of the key themes have already emerged. You have highlighted very clearly the benefits of electrification – decarbonisation of our economy and our society being chief among them – and the benefit of energy security, the need for which has been underlined once again for us by geopolitical developments outside of our control.

But you've also highlighted the importance of competitiveness and how the electrification of our economy and of industry can bring significant competitiveness benefits, but on the basis of one proviso, and that is that we make improvements on the question of affordability and that electrification leads to more affordable energy for our citizens, but also for industry.

That is ultimately the key litmus test, and it is important that we work together to ensure that this is the case. Indeed, by providing the upfront investment and by coordinated action across the European Union, we do believe that we can achieve that.

In terms of the detail of the Electrification Action Plan, it is currently being finalised by the Commission and we aim for adoption before the summer recess. So it's too early to discuss the details of the concrete measures that do remain under development, but we welcome the ideas and the recommendations from the Parliament.

On the one hand, the Electrification Action Plan will integrate an electrification target. The target framing needs to be ambitious. It will be supported by measures to overcome barriers and put us on an ambitious electrification track. Some measures will be horizontal and others will be sector specific – for example, targeting transport, buildings and industry.

We intend to follow a value-chain approach and to support business models in Europe. The Commission will, inter alia, propose action to lower the electricity fossil-fuels price ratio, and measures to accelerate the uptake of electrification solutions, such as through a market-based instrument on heat pumps. This includes phasing out fossil fuel subsidies, which undermine the relative competitiveness of electricity vis-à-vis other energy carriers. Again, the question of the comparative cost of electricity vis-à-vis gas is one where we need to make progress, for sure.

The Commission will adopt a legal proposal on network charges and taxation. The proposal will provide incentives to make an optimal and cost-effective use of the grid, while ensuring that electricity is taxed less than gas. Electrification of key sectors means lowering import dependencies on fossil fuels and improving our energy security.

While the EU has achieved already a lot in transforming the electricity mix into a mix of abundant and clean sources – 70 % renewables and nuclear – this is not the case in sectors such as industry, transport and buildings, which continue to be dominated still today by imported fossil fuels. This needs to change, and how we approach the design of an electricity target will be designed to ensure that this is achieved.

Increasing the share of home-grown clean energy and the share of electricity in key sectors, where technically and economically viable, requires reinforcing our energy system flexibility through, crucially, more interconnectors, grids, storage and demand response, as some of you have already highlighted.

So, the electrification target, supported by measures that enable reaching it – because a target is only as good as the measures that underpin how we will deliver it – will provide a clear political signal and take into account the key performance indicator of the Clean Industrial Deal.
So those nuts and bolts are really important: interconnectors, grids, storage and demand response.

In addition, we already have had mention in the debate this afternoon concerning nuclear, and as we know, colleagues, the precise energy mix is a matter for the Member States concerned. But we need all clean sources of energy to achieve the objective of reducing our dependence on fossil fuels, while keeping system costs in check and strengthening grid stability. Next to renewables, nuclear remains the other core component of our domestic supply of clean electricity, and we should use our existing power generation efficiently and look at new technologies such as small modular reactors.

So, I look forward to the remainder of the debate. As I say, the key issues have already been touched on: decarbonisation, energy security, affordability and improving competitiveness. But to achieve all of this will require a collective effort on behalf of all of the institutions to make these ambitions a reality. I look forward to the remaining contributions.

paragraphs.text: Г-н Председател, г-н Комисар, колеги, през 1920 г. болшевишкият диктатор Ленин е казал, че комунизмът е електрификация плюс съветска власт. Може би оттогава започва твърде лошата традиция да превръщаме практичния разговор за енергетика в идеологически конфликт, както се случва между другото и днес.
Крайните фракции в този Парламент водят културна война, въоръжени с клишета, а не прагматичен спор, основан на факти.

Но нека да погледнем фактите. Те са, че навсякъде, където електрификацията на индустрията и транспорта се развива успешно, и това без съмнение е нещо много хубаво — от Швеция на север до Испания на юг, Франция, Чили в Южното полукълбо, а и дори комунистически Китай, това успешно развитие е опряно на няколко фактора и нито един от тях не е тежка регулация, амбициозни политически цели, още по-малко идеологически догми. Те са на първо място качествен електрически микс, основан и на възобновяеми източници, и на базови мощности, най-често силна ядрена енергетика, и преди всичко пазар на очевидно ниски цени на енергията. Това е посоката, в която трябва да насочим нашия план, а не към тежки регулации. И със сигурност, надявам се, не към съветска власт.

political_group.label: PPE
political_group.name: Group of the European People's Party (Christian Democrats)

paragraphs.text: Mr President, Commissioner, colleagues, Europe cannot electrify its future with grids built for the past. This is especially true in south-eastern Europe, from Bulgaria to Greece and Romania. Our region has enormous potential for clean power industry and cross‑border trade. But potential does not lower bills, potential does not power factories and potential does not reach citizens unless the infrastructure is there.

Today, too much clean energy is blocked by bottlenecks, delayed by weak grids or made too expensive by outdated tariffs and charges. So the Electrification Action Plan must be a plan of delivery: to build the grids, to fix the tariffs and charges, to put storage flexibility and demand response in the centre; and to protect consumers, because those costs cannot be transmitted to households and industry. Electrification is not an ideology: it is Europe's road to affordable energy and to industrial strength.

political_group.label: S&D
political_group.name: Group of the Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats in the European Parliament

paragraphs.text: Mr President, Commissioner, it is realistic to increase the electrification of some industrial processes and also heat supply, but the affordable price of electricity and capacities meeting demands is a key condition. And let's be honest, the demand will grow, through AI, cars, heat pumps – it has been mentioned already. But before we have the required installed capacity in renewable and nuclear, we will use both local and imported fossil fuels. That's it.

One example: to produce one megawatt-hour of lignite coal electricity in the EU costs EUR 10, but we add through carbon allowances – emission allowances – EUR 70 more. So to do more and enable more electrification in the EU, with affordable electricity, we must for some given time also cut the prices of coal and gas electricity.
So I would like to call on you, Commissioner, to reintroduce the free allocations for electricity producers from coal, lignite and gas until the time that we will not need these sources anymore.

paragraphs.text: Panie Przewodniczący! Komisja przedstawia całkowicie nierealistyczny i utopijny plan, którego realizacja pogłębi zapaść gospodarczą i doprowadzi do zubożenia Europy. Czego dziś potrzebuje Europa? Taniej energii, konkurencyjnego przemysłu, rozwoju gospodarczego.

Postulaty dekarbonizacji, odejścia od paliw kopalnych i zarządzania centralnego z Brukseli są sprzeczne z tymi celami. Zamiast likwidować tradycyjne źródła energii, należy niezwłocznie wycofać się z Zielonego Ładu i systemu ETS, które drenują kieszenie obywateli i hamują gospodarkę.

Europa będzie się rozwijać, kiedy sfery wolności gospodarczej i obywatelskiej będą poszerzane. Narzucanie przez Brukselę kolejnych biurokratycznych ograniczeń i realizowanie polityki decydowania o sprawach krajów członkowskich jest gwarancją regresu i zapaści gospodarczej. Europa nie potrzebuje ośrodka decyzyjnego w Brukseli. Europa nie potrzebuje ideologicznych zielonych szaleństw. Europa potrzebuje więcej wolności i rozsądku.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, I don't understand what we are waiting for. Of course, we need to electrify. That's what's needed for jobs, economy, climate. And of course, we need an electrification target. Otherwise, Europe completely lags behind globally.

But I have to address something very important: if we are to electrify the system completely, the system needs to work. And right now, the German electricity market is not working. This has been going on for too long. The catastrophic situation on the German electricity market now impacts Swedish consumers. The Swedes in the south end up paying unacceptable high energy prices, as a consequence of German energy policy. That ends up impacting the acceptance of the EU's electrification.
I beg you, please take care of your problem: split Germany into bidding zones so that electrification gets the chance to actually work.
Ich meine euch, Deutschland. Bitte hört zu!

paragraphs.text: Madame la Présidente, il était temps. Il était temps que notre Parlement se saisisse de l'électrification, car notre dépendance aux énergies fossiles est mortifère. Soyons clairs: chaque chaudière remplacée, chaque usine décarbonée, c'est de la souveraineté retrouvée. C'est aussi un coup d'arrêt aux 60 milliards d'euros d'importations en énergies fossiles qui appauvrissent la France chaque année, comme toute l'Union européenne.

Donc électrifier, oui, mais avec quel courage politique? Vouloir une transition massive vers l'électricité en restant soumis aux lois du marché, c'est un non-sens économique et écologique. Comment défendre le pouvoir d'achat et le climat si notre électricité décarbonée dépend toujours de la spéculation du prix du gaz au niveau international. Partons d'un constat simple. La libéralisation du secteur de l'énergie est un échec. Elle a fait exploser les prix. Elle a ralenti la création de capacités de production et elle freine aujourd'hui des chantiers du siècle, alors que 80 millions de kilomètres de lignes électriques doivent être déployées dans le monde pour des besoins de raccordement.

L'indépendance exige donc de sortir des énergies fossiles, oui, mais aussi des investissements massifs et un retour au contrôle public de l'énergie. En conclusion, l'électrification est notre plus grande force, mais elle exige un préalable: reprendre la main et sortir des logiques de marché.

Negli ultimi venti anni, in Italia, spendendo la bellezza di 70 miliardi di euro, abbiamo installato impianti eolici e fotovoltaici per una potenza di 60 gigawatt, il che ci consente di produrre – look at me, Commissioner – solo il 4 % del fabbisogno energetico globale nazionale, solo il 4 %. Questi impianti sono chiaramente incentivati robustamente, il che ci rivela che non sono convenienti, altrimenti non avrebbero bisogno di incentivi.

Ecco, allora, usciamo dal corto circuito della decarbonizzazione e ricominciamo a produrre energia nel modo più conveniente, evitando così di arricchire le multinazionali del Green Deal, la finanza internazionale e la Cina.

paragraphs.text: Vážená pani predsedajúca, energetika je otázkou bezpečnosti, konkurencieschopnosti, ale aj sociálnej stability v Európskej únii. V Európe sme pomaly zničili priemysel, v ktorom sme desaťročia vynikali a bol nám na prospech. Nahradili sme ho priemyslom, pre ktorý nedokážeme vyrobiť technológie. Nemáme surovinové základňu, ale čo je hlavné, chýba nám elektrická infraštruktúra, pretože tá naša je 50 rokov zastaralá, nemá adekvátnu kapacitu.

Európska komisia sľubuje lacnú energiu, dátové centrá, kvantové technológie, robotiku, dekarbonizovaný priemysel a konkurencieschopnosť. Ale bez moderných elektrických sietí sú to len prázdne sľuby. V roku 2024 stáli núdzové zásahy pri riadení preťažených sietí približne 4,3 miliardy eur. To je súčet za systém, ktorý nestíha realitu a už absolútne nestíha nerealistické ambície.

Preto nový viacročný finančný rámec je posledným možným momentom na zmenu kurzu. Musíme urobiť nasledovné: odstrániť byrokratické bariéry, zrýchliť povoľovacie procesy a sústrediť investície do základnej energetickej infraštruktúry, interkonektorov, skladovania a odolnosti energetického odvetvia.

paragraphs.text: Sehr geehrte Frau Präsidentin, sehr geehrter Herr Kommissar! Die Elektrifizierung Europas begann nicht mit einem Aktionsplan. Sie begann mit Erfindergeist, mit Wissenschaft, mit Unternehmertum, und aus den ersten Experimenten mit Elektrizität wurden im 19. Jahrhundert Stromnetze, elektrische Beleuchtung, Straßenbahnen, Fabriken, moderne Industrie – und hier drinnen wäre es ganz schön dunkel ohne Elektrizität. Elektrifizierung ist eine europäische Fortschrittsgeschichte, weil Energie plötzlich verfügbar, nutzbar und produktiv wurde, und genau daran müssen wir die heutige Energiepolitik messen.

Im Februar 2025 hatte die Kommission den Aktionsplan für erschwingliche Energie verkündet mit dem Versprechen, Energie für Bürger und Unternehmen wieder bezahlbar zu machen, aber heute müssen wir uns ehrlich fragen, was davon angekommen ist. Familien schauen nicht auf Aktionspläne, sondern auf die Stromrechnung, auf die Tankrechnung; und Mittelstand und Industrie entscheiden nicht nach Aktionsplänen, sondern danach, ob sich Investitionen in Europa noch rechnen – und dabei ist die Realität schwierig geblieben. Energie ist nach wie vor eines der größten Standortprobleme Europas.

Und nun kommt der nächste Aktionsplan, der Aktionsplan für Elektrifizierung, und deshalb meine Frage: Können Sie sicherstellen, dass dieser neue Aktionsplan nicht nur weitere verbindliche Elektrifizierungsziele enthält und Pflichten, sondern das Standortproblem Europas wirklich adressiert?

Elektrifizierung kann und muss wieder eine europäische Fortschrittsgeschichte werden, aber nur dann, wenn sie Wettbewerbsfähigkeit ermöglicht und die Versprechen an unsere Bürgerinnen und Bürger wirklich erfüllt.

paragraphs.text: Andrea, we share the same passion for electrification, I have no doubt. But the latest analysis from ACER is really showing that the German electricity market is not functioning well. The preferred design of the market would be to split Germany into five pricing zones, so that we have proper pricing, reflecting the actual situation in each of the different parts of Germany.

Why is this not happening? Why is Germany not listening to the advice from the European agencies and taking this into account so that we have a functioning electricity market, which we need in order to electrify?

paragraphs.text: Madam President, friends, we have a problem, obviously, with our dependency on the foreign fossil fuels we import for billions every day. When we import from the Middle East, from Vladimir Putin, from the United States. When we import gas and oil that we do not have ourselves. So, we need to import 98 % of the gas and oil that we consume here in Europe from abroad.

I think it is absolutely crazy that colleagues here in this room seriously think that it is a good idea to keep on doing that. They reject investments in renewable energy. We have the possibility to produce our own energy – our home-grown energy – here in Europe. That means that we need to invest more in electrification, solar panels, wind turbines, heat pumps. And we can do that and we can become independent and we can combat climate change at the same time.
It's not a good strategy to be dependent on dictators from foreign countries. It's a good strategy to invest in our own industry. We should do that.

Az iparban ezért az innovációt, a lakóépületek esetében az energetikai korszerűsítést, a közlekedésnél pedig a töltőhálózat kiépítését kell ösztönözni. Az áramhálózat fejlesztése is elengedhetetlen. Ennek csökkentésére el kell indítani a kapcsolódó képzési támogatási programokat.
