interventions.speaker_label: Magnus Brunner, Member of the Commission.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, honourable Members, in Burkina Faso, the values you were talking about, like democracy, like the rule of law, human rights and others are challenged, to put it very politely. We see pressure of terrorist groups and the tense security and humanitarian situation, and we also see an implementation of a wider political agenda based on the refoundation of state and society as the current military regime has systematically restricted freedoms of expression, association and also political participation.

We have also seen that political parties and civil society organisations have been dissolved, and journalists, activists and critics have been targeted with arbitrary arrests, with detentions, disappearances and also forced conscription. There has been some openness, on the one hand, by the government regarding the dialogue and cooperation on specific matters, including human rights protection. But on the other hand, regrettably, the authorities have also in recent months demonstrated less tolerance and acceptance of divergent voices concerning the strain on human rights in the country.

This situation in Burkina Faso calls for a clear sighted and also pragmatic approach to the EU's engagement in Burkina Faso. Mindful of these developments, the European Union intends to continue its sustained and constructive diplomatic engagement, coupled with unwavering support for civil society and human rights defenders.

In line with the renewed approach for the Sahel, the EU's special representative for the region visited the country several times, three times altogether, and recognised the significant challenges but also the opportunities worth pursuing with the authorities. He also raised the issues of values, the shrinking of civic space and human rights violations with his counterparts, in a spirit of open and respectful dialogue. He is planning, by the way, to travel to Burkina Faso one last time, in a few days' time, before the end of his term of office.

According to our experience in the region, we strongly believe this balance between defending universal values and pragmatic engagement on the ground could offer the most effective pathway to preserving space for dialogue and for cooperation. Our purpose is to contribute positively to the country and also its population. Our interests, of course, need to match. We are convinced that the effective respect and promotion of human rights is an integral part of this effort.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, all the abuses that were mentioned here, and all the accusations of severe violations of human rights happening in Burkina Faso, they are true. But they are just the effects, unfortunately, because after 2022, the relationship between Burkina Faso and Russia got closer and closer. Today, Russia is offering military training, weapons and diplomatic support to this military junta that is currently controlling the country.

I think it is important – besides supporting all these people in Burkina Faso and NGOs and everybody there – to really have a pragmatic approach to this situation, because, exactly as we had with the other debate about Belarus, what is happening in Burkina Faso is not only the situation in the world. We have to find a way to pragmatically and realistically approach this situation and find ways to correct it by engaging with these people, obviously without violating and jeopardising and compromising our values and principles.

political_group.name: Group of the European People's Party (Christian Democrats)

paragraphs.text: Κυρία Πρόεδρε, οι σοσιαλοδημοκράτες και τα άλλα αστικά κόμματα, νέοι και αναπαλαιωμένοι σωτήρες, έσπειραν αυταπάτες για το —πλέον ενεργοποιημένο— σύμφωνο μετανάστευσης και ασύλου, όπως κάνουν και για το ανύπαρκτο κράτος δικαίου της Ευρωπαϊκής Ένωσης. Οι κανονισμοί του συμφώνου, που είναι και πυλώνες του νέου αντιδραστικού νόμου στην Ελλάδα της Νέας Δημοκρατίας, προωθούν την καταστολή για νέα εγκλήματα, όπως αυτό —χωρίς τιμωρία— στην Πύλο, τις λεγόμενες «επιστροφές», δηλαδή απελάσεις, που αποτελούν ενταφιασμό της Συνθήκης της Γενεύης, με απάνθρωπο εκτοπισμό σε στρατόπεδα συγκέντρωσης τρίτων χωρών. Οι δε κατευθύνσεις για νόμιμες οδούς μετανάστευσης σημαίνουν διακρατικές συμφωνίες εργασιακής γαλέρας μεταναστών ως πάμφθηνο εργατικό δυναμικό για το κεφάλαιο.

Όσο για τα περί ασφαλών τρίτων χωρών, συνιστούν ξέπλυμα των εταίρων της Ευρωπαϊκής Ένωσης, των τζιχαντιστών στη Συρία, των Ταλιμπάν στο Αφγανιστάν, για να γυρίζουν τους ξεριζωμένους πίσω στη φωτιά ενός πολέμου που η ίδια η Ευρωπαϊκή Ένωση και οι σύμμαχοί της έσπειραν.

Απαιτούμε την κατάργηση του συμφώνου, την υλοποίηση της Συνθήκης της Γενεύης, την προστασία όλων των παιδιών ανεξαιρέτως, χαρτιά και δικαιώματα σε πρόσφυγες και μετανάστες για τις χώρες τελικού προορισμού. Καμιά πολεμική εμπλοκή («…»).

paragraphs.text: Señora presidenta, señor comisario, la aprobación definitiva del Reglamento sobre el Retorno ha sido celebrada en esta sesión del Parlamento Europeo con un aplauso en pie de todos los grupos de la extrema derecha de este Parlamento que han formado mayoría con el Partido Popular.
Creo que eso lo dice todo, además de sus gritos «send them back», es decir, «devuélvanlos» porque no pertenecen a la Unión Europea aunque se encuentren en situación vulnerable.

El Reglamento sobre el Retorno no forma parte del Pacto sobre Migración y Asilo, ¿verdad? No, al contrario, está fuera de su perímetro. Pero es que además contradice el objeto del Pacto sobre Migración y Asilo, que era crear obligaciones legales para todos los Estados miembros con una legislación europea vinculante. Porque lo que hace el Reglamento sobre el Retorno es permitir que bilateralmente cada Estado miembro pueda contratar con el gobernante de un país tercero, sin ninguna conexión significativa con las personas —que de eso se trata, de seres humanos—, con tal de que se los mantenga fuera de nuestra vista a cambio de dinero.

No solamente es una negación del Pacto sobre Migración y Asilo, sino que es una negación de los valores europeos, de la Carta de los Derechos Fundamentales de la Unión Europea y hasta del alma de Europa.

political_group.label: S&D
political_group.name: Group of the Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats in the European Parliament

paragraphs.text: Pani Przewodnicząca! Cieszę się, że dzisiaj Parlament Europejski wykonał ważny krok w kierunku zapewnienia bezpieczeństwa wszystkim mieszkańcom Europy. Te przepisy, które dzisiaj zostały przyjęte, pozwalają wreszcie w sposób legalny deportować te osoby, które dostały się do Europy w sposób nieuprawniony. Osoby, które tutaj dostały się w sposób nielegalny. Dobrze, że Parlament Europejski wreszcie miał odwagę – po wielu latach apeli ze strony prawicy – do tego, aby przyjąć te przepisy. Cieszę się, że lewica przegrała wreszcie tę batalię, bo oni od lat rozszczelniali system bezpieczeństwa całej Europy.

Mam nadzieję również, że te przepisy będą konsekwentnie wykorzystywane przez państwa Unii Europejskiej do tego, aby faktycznie deportować z terenu Unii Europejskiej te osoby, które w nielegalny sposób się tutaj dostały.

Mam nadzieję również, że Parlamentowi w przyszłości wystarczy odwagi, żeby wyłączyć stosowanie, żeby w ogóle usunąć z przepisów pakt migracyjny, tak aby ta polityka wreszcie siłowego przemieszczania ludzi wewnątrz Unii Europejskiej również się zakończyła.

political_group.label: PPE
political_group.name: Group of the European People's Party (Christian Democrats)

paragraphs.text: Madam President, I voted in favour of the report on Türkiye, because the European Union must pursue a pragmatic and strategic relationship with one of its most important neighbouring countries. Türkiye is a key partner of the EU on a wide range of issues. Regarding security and defence, Türkiye has the second largest military force in NATO and plays a crucial role in safeguarding the alliance's southern flank and contributing to regional stability.

Türkiye is also an indispensable partner in managing migration flows, combating organised crime and addressing common security challenges. While differences remain between the EU and Türkiye on certain issues, the European Union should move away from an approach centred primarily on criticism and political lecturing to a pragmatic one, recognising positive developments, encouraging constructive cooperation and focusing on areas of converging interests. Engagement, dialogue and partnership are far more effective than isolation in advancing stability, prosperity and mutual understanding.

political_group.label: PPE
political_group.name: Group of the European People's Party (Christian Democrats)

paragraphs.text: Doamnă președintă, am votat în favoarea raportului privind Albania, deoarece susțin că locul Albaniei este în Uniunea Europeană. Procesul de extindere reprezintă unul dintre cele mai importante instrumente prin care UE contribuie la stabilitatea, prosperitatea și dezvoltarea demografică a regiunii Balcanilor de Vest. Raportul reflectă aceste evoluții pozitive și recunoaște eforturile depuse de autoritățile albaneze pentru implementarea reformelor necesare în domenii esențiale precum statul de drept, administrația publică și consolidarea instituțiilor democratice.

În același timp, este important să recunoaștem că există încă provocări care trebuie abordate, inclusiv în ceea ce privește punerea în aplicare efectivă a hotărârilor definitive ale instanțelor de judecată. Din acest motiv, salut decizia Guvernului Albaniei de a pune în aplicare, în sfârșit, hotărârea definitivă privind retrocedarea către România a Casei Iorga, un simbol al relațiilor istorice și culturale dintre cele două state.
Ca europarlamentar, am solicitat insistent autorităților albaneze să restituie României Casa Iorga și mă aștept ca aceasta să fie restituită până în septembrie 2026, așa cum s-a promis.

political_group.name: Group of the European People's Party (Christian Democrats)

paragraphs.text: Gospa predsednica, to poročilo je poročilo o evropski prihodnosti makedonske države. Zakaj sem ga na koncu podprla – čeprav seveda ne teksta v celoti? Zato, ker ta država ni odgovorna za obsedenost nekaterih z njenim narodom.

Človek se res vpraša, a veste: kdo ima tukaj problem v resnici? Makedonci ali tisti, ki brez njih ne znajo napisati niti amandmaja, kaj šele vsebinskega? Potem pa še vlagajo vso energijo v neke razlage, kdo je kdo. Precej nenavaden hobi za leto 2026, mar ne? Interpretacija preteklosti. Kaj smo mi, zgodovinska akademija ali Evropski parlament?

Evropska unija je nastala zato, da bi narodi skupaj gradili prihodnost. Ne zato, da bi si med seboj izdajali potrdila o obstoju. In zagotovo ne zato, da bi stari nacionalizmi spet dobili evropski oder, po možnosti čim bolj modernega.
(govori v jeziku, ki ni uradni jezik EU)

paragraphs.text: Doamnă președintă, „Iovanovici” este chiar nume de acolo, din Serbia, de lângă Kosovo. Am votat împotriva acestui raport și este inacceptabil și jignitor și un atac inacceptabil la suveranitatea și independența Serbiei să vorbiți despre Kosovo.

Bunicul meu patern este născut exact în Serbia, lângă Kosovo. Niciodată Serbia și noi, românii, nu vom accepta Kosovo. Nici poporul român, nici România nu a recunoscut Kosovo. Kosovo nu există ca stat și vă rog frumos să încetați să vă mai referiți la Kosovo.

Vreți ca Serbia să adere la Uniunea Europeană în timp ce dumneavoastră o măcelăriți? Și să vă mai spun ce ați făcut cu această chestiune, cu Kosovo. Inclusiv Putin când a spus că el își vrea Donbasul și Luganskul pentru că există precedentul Kosovo pe care dumneavoastră l-ați rupt de la corpul-mamă Serbiei. Niciodată în viața dumneavoastră să nu vă mai permiteți să vorbiți de Kosovo. Kosovo e Serbia! Kosovo e Serbia!
